sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which drivers must hold a permit or license before operating on public roads in Iowa?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Any person who drives a car, motorcycle, or moped on public roads in Iowa must hold a permit or license.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: When may an armed-forces member drive in Iowa without holding an Iowa driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Service members driving military vehicles while on duty do not need an Iowa license.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Under what distance and trip limit may farm machinery use Iowa roads without a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.memory_hook: Home farm trips within two miles
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Farm machinery may move between the home farm and nearby fields or farm sites within two miles with no license needed.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: What credential lets an out-of-state visitor or student legally drive on Iowa roadways?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Visitors and students may drive in Iowa on a valid license from their home state or country.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How does Iowa's military exemption change when a service member switches from an on-duty rig to a personal car?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: Military members are exempt only while driving military vehicles on duty; the same person driving a personal car needs an Iowa credential.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: When does driving farm equipment on public roads in Iowa require a valid driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Farm equipment is exempt only between the home farm and nearby land within two miles; other farm driving on public roads needs a license.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: How does registering to vote in Iowa affect your residency status for driver licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Registering to vote in Iowa counts you as a resident for driver licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: What happens to your driver-licensing status when you enroll a child in an Iowa public school?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Enrolling a child in an Iowa public school counts you as a resident for driver licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: How does accepting permanent employment in Iowa change your status for driver licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Taking a permanent job in Iowa counts you as a resident for driver licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: How many unbroken days of living in Iowa make you a resident for driver-licensing rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Living in Iowa without a break for thirty days counts you as a resident for driver licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Which two property tax exemption claims count you as an Iowa resident for driver licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Claiming a homestead or military tax exemption on Iowa property counts you as a resident for driver licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: What does receiving state public assistance mean for your Iowa driver-licensing residency?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Getting public assistance from the state counts you as a resident for driver licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: How many residency conditions must you meet before Iowa counts you as a resident for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Meeting any single one of the residency triggers is enough to count as an Iowa resident for licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does a newcomer's licensing status shift once they reach thirty continuous days in Iowa?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: A newcomer with no residency trigger yet may drive as a visitor on a home license, while thirty continuous days in Iowa makes that same newcomer a resident.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Why can someone become an Iowa resident on day one without waiting thirty continuous days?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The thirty-day clock is only one of the residency triggers, so voting, schooling, a job, a tax exemption, or state aid can make you a resident on day one.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Do you have to claim both homestead and military property tax exemptions to trigger Iowa residency?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: The homestead and military tax exemptions are alternative triggers, so claiming either one alone is enough for residency.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: When are you required to carry your driver's license or learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Keep your license or permit with you every time you drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Besides your license or permit, which two documents must stay with the vehicle in paper or digital form?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Motorists must also keep current registration proof plus a paper or electronic insurance card showing liability coverage.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: What two penalties can strike if you get pulled over without required license, registration, or insurance proof?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Missing paperwork can mean fines and possible impoundment of your vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: What distinct legal fact does each of your three required driving documents prove at a traffic stop?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Your license proves you may drive, while the registration and insurance card prove the vehicle is legal and covered; all three must ride along.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Which physical screening must every applicant complete when applying for an Iowa driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Every applicant must complete a vision screening when applying for a license.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which exam must every applicant pass before qualifying for an Iowa driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Every applicant must pass the knowledge test to qualify for a license.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Which age group must prove completion of a state-approved driver education course to get licensed?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Drivers younger than eighteen must show they finished a state-approved driver education course.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: When can an Iowa license applicant skip taking a separate behind-the-wheel driving evaluation?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: A behind-the-wheel driving test is required unless you already satisfied the driver education course requirement.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Which special licensing program governs Iowa drivers under age eighteen, with full rules posted online?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen are covered by the Graduated Driver's License Program, with details on the DOT website.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Between the knowledge check and the behind-the-wheel drive, which one can driver education waive and which never drops?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The knowledge test can never be waived, while the driving test drops away once the driver education course requirement is met.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How does the manual distinguish completing the vision screening from taking the knowledge requirement?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: The vision screening is a check completed at application time, while the knowledge test is an exam that must be passed.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How do state-approved driver education and the Graduated Driver's License Program differ for under-eighteen drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Driver education is a course drivers under eighteen must finish, while the Graduated Driver's License Program is the separate under-eighteen program named on the same page.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What free study resource does the Iowa DOT post on its website to help applicants prepare?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: Iowa DOT publishes an online practice test on its website to help you study for the knowledge test.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What does Iowa's Skip the Trip program allow eligible applicants to complete from home or school?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Iowa offers a Skip the Trip option for taking the knowledge test at home or school, with details on the DOT website.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: How does Iowa treat moped credentials and commercial credentials compared with a standard license?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Moped licenses and commercial licenses are separate license types with their own requirements on the DOT website.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: Where does the Iowa driver's manual direct motorists to find current timing and steps for license renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: The handbook sends readers to the DOT website for when and how to renew a license.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: How does the DOT online study tool differ from Iowa's Skip the Trip option?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: The online practice test only prepares you, while Skip the Trip is a real way to sit the knowledge test at home or school.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: How are rectangular rapid-flashing beacons activated, and at what kinds of crossings are they installed?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Rectangular rapid-flashing beacons switch on by push button and usually sit at crossings with no traffic signal or at mid-block crosswalks.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What two duties kick in the instant a crosswalk beacon's amber lights start strobing?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: While the beacon amber lamps strobe, halt for anybody inside the crosswalk and watch for anybody about to step into it.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: On a pedestrian hybrid beacon, what do dark lenses, a blinking bottom yellow, and a steady bottom yellow tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.memory_hook: Dark proceed, blink slow, steady prepare
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon sleeps dark until a walker triggers it; dark lamps mean drive through carefully, a blinking lower yellow means ease off, and a steady lower yellow means get ready to halt.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: How does your stop duty change when a hybrid beacon's twin top reds shift from steady to alternating blink?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Once the beacon twin upper reds glow steady, stop for the crossing pedestrians; when they start blinking, stop if you have not yet done so, then roll on carefully if the crossing stands empty.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How does a rectangular rapid-flashing beacon's light pattern differ from a pedestrian hybrid beacon?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The rapid-flashing beacon answers a button with strobing amber at signal-free crossings, while the hybrid beacon answers a walker with a yellow-to-red lamp ladder.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Why doesn't an unlit pedestrian hybrid beacon act like a broken four-way stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: A dark hybrid beacon invites careful passage, while steady twin reds on the same beacon command a stop for pedestrians.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How does proceeding past strobing amber beacons compare with proceeding under blinking twin red hybrid lamps?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Under strobing amber you stay stopped for crosswalk users, while under blinking twin reds you stop once and may roll on through an empty crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: Which two mobility aids identify a pedestrian who is likely blind and needs extra driver caution?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Treat a person guided by a harnessed service dog or tapping a white or white-and-red cane as likely blind, and drive with added care to keep them safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: How does Iowa traffic law frame right-of-way when road users meet without signs or signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Where no signs or signals govern a meeting of road users, yield rules pick who waits; the law names who must yield but hands the right-of-way to nobody.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What overriding duty applies even when the other driver or walker clearly should have yielded to you?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Whoever holds the right-of-way, still do all you can to keep from hitting a pedestrian or another car.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How do Iowa's statutory yield rules pair with every driver's duty to prevent a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Yield rules name who waits but award the right-of-way to no one, while the crash-avoidance duty binds even whoever holds it.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Why should you yield to a bicyclist even when traffic rules say the rider ought to wait for you?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Bikes and cars share the same road rights and duties, yet riders crash unprotected, so drive defensively and yield to them even on occasions they should yield to you.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: What explains giving extra defensive leeway to cyclists who hold the exact same legal duties as cars?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Cyclists carry the same road rights as drivers, yet draw extra yielding because they crash unprotected.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Which single driving mistake causes more fatal traffic crashes in Iowa than any other?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Failing to yield the right-of-way ranks as the top cause of deadly traffic crashes in Iowa.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: What three conditions must all line up before you turn right at a steady red light?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: After a full stop you may turn right on red unless a sign bans it, yielding as you go.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Who holds priority when you want to turn left across an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: A left-turning driver waits for oncoming cars bound straight ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How does what you wait for on a right-on-red turn compare with a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Right on red needs only a stop and a yield unless a sign bans it, while a left turn must wait out straight-bound oncoming cars.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: How do arrival order and tie-breakers work after stopping completely at an all-way stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: At an all-way stop the first car to arrive leaves first after stopping fully, and when cars arrive together the one on the right moves first.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What separates staggered arrivals from tied arrivals at an all-way stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: First to the all-way stop leaves first, while simultaneous arrivals send the rightmost car first.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Who takes priority whenever your tires cross a sidewalk at an alley, lot, or driveway?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Crossing a sidewalk or rolling into or out of a driveway, alley, or lot, give way to people on foot.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: What is the legal difference between crossing a sidewalk and driving along one?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Wheels may cross a sidewalk but may never travel along it.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Who gets priority when you pull onto a street from a shoulder, alley, or private driveway?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Pulling onto a road from a driveway, alley, or shoulder, yield to traffic already rolling there.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Pulling out of a driveway across a sidewalk onto a street, which two yields happen back-to-back?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Entering the road you yield to rolling traffic, while crossing the sidewalk you yield to people on foot.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Do pedestrian crosswalk rights depend on whether white lines are painted on the asphalt?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Stop or yield for pedestrians in marked crossings and in unmarked ones alike.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How must you approach an intersection that has zero stop signs or traffic lights?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: With no stop sign or signal, every driver slows and enters with care, all the controlled-intersection rules still bind, and extra caution rules.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: What stays identical and what increases at an unsigned intersection compared with a signed one?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: Signed intersections spell the rules out, while unsigned ones bind the same rules plus extra caution.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: Which lights or sounds on police, fire, ambulance, or rescue vehicles trigger your duty to yield?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Give way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency rigs sounding a siren or horn or flashing red or blue.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Where do you steer when an active emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Spotting or hearing one approach from any side, ease to the right road edge or as close right as you can get.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: How do you handle an approaching emergency rig if you are mid-intersection or across a physical median?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Caught inside an intersection or roundabout, drive through it before pulling aside; but on a median-split road with the rig across the divider, you need not stop at all.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Why does pulling right immediately on an open street change to driving forward first inside an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Open road means ease right for the rig at once, while sitting inside an intersection means drive through it before pulling aside.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: What minimum distance must you keep behind an emergency vehicle running lights and siren?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Hang back at least five hundred feet behind a rig running lights and siren.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Compare your duty across a median divider from an emergency rig against driving behind that same rig?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Across a median divider you need not stop for the rig at all, while trailing one you must keep five hundred feet back.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Following a school bus on a two- or three-lane road, what do flashing amber or red lamps forbid?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Trailing a bus on a two- or three-lane road, its flashing red or amber lamps forbid passing and order readiness to stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: How far behind a stopped school bus with its arm extended must you halt, and when may you move?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Once that bus halts with its stop arm swung out, stop no closer than fifteen feet behind the bus and wait until the arm retracts and the bus moves again, then proceed carefully.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: Meeting an oncoming school bus flashing amber lights on an undivided two- or three-lane road, what speed cap applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Facing the bus as its amber lamps blink, slow to no more than twenty miles per hour and prepare to stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: When that oncoming bus on a two- or three-lane road extends its stop arm, what must you do?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: When the oncoming bus stops with its arm extended, halt ahead of it, stay put until the arm retracts, and roll on with care.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: How do amber school-bus lights restrict a trailing driver differently from an oncoming driver?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: From behind, flashing bus lamps forbid passing outright, while from ahead amber lamps only slow you to no more than twenty miles per hour

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: How long can Iowa suspend your driver's license for illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Breaking the school-bus stopping law can cost you your license for up to one hundred eighty days.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: Pair the minimum stopping distance behind a school bus with the maximum license suspension for violating it?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: The halted bus demands fifteen feet of queue space behind it, while a violation can suspend your license for up to one hundred eighty days.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Does adding four or more lanes change your stopping duty when you are traveling behind a school bus?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Trailing the bus on four-plus lanes, obey the same drill: never pass on flashing red or amber, stop behind the halted bus with its arm out keeping at least fifteen feet back, and wait until the arm retracts and the bus moves.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: What is the single situation in Iowa where you may pass a stopped school bus with its arm out?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: Meeting the bus across opposite lanes on a four-or-more-lane road, you may roll past without stopping even with its lamps flashing and arm out, the single lawful pass of a stopped, armed bus.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: Meeting an oncoming armed school bus, how does moving from three lanes to four lanes flip Iowa's rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: Facing the armed bus on a narrow road you must halt ahead of it, while facing it across a wide road you may roll past.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: On a four-lane road, why does one side stop for an armed school bus while the opposite side keeps rolling?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: From behind on a wide road you stop and wait like on a narrow one, while from ahead across the lanes you are released.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: When does safe driving begin, and what guide sets your vehicle's maintenance schedule?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Safe arrival starts before ignition with both driver and car ready; steady upkeep saves cash, aids emergencies, and follows the owner manual schedule.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How many independent brake systems must cars, trucks, and ATVs or UTVs have versus motorcycles and mopeds?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Cars, trucks, and ATVs or UTVs need twin braking systems, foot plus parking brake, while motorcycles and mopeds need at least one.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Which four brake warning signs mean your vehicle needs a mechanic right away?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Weak braking, noisy brakes, odd brake odor, or a pedal sinking to the floor all send you to a mechanic.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Pair what guides routine vehicle maintenance with how brake-system requirements split by vehicle type?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Upkeep follows the owner manual schedule, while brake counts follow vehicle kind: twin systems for cars and ATVs, one for bikes.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: When brakes grind, smell odd, or sink underfoot, what is the single safe move?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Noise, odor, and sinking pedals are the brake warnings, while a mechanic visit is the only response.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: How do you confirm that headlights, taillights, brake lamps, and turn signals actually light up?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Verify signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights by walking around outside the car.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What front, rear, and license-plate lights must every car, truck, and street-used ATV or UTV carry?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Every car, truck, and ATV or UTV carries two front headlights, left and right, plus at least one rear red lamp seen for five hundred feet and a white lamp lighting the rear plate.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What applies to any installed turn signals, and at what vehicle or trailer width are electric signals mandatory?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Fitted turn signals must function, and signals are mandatory on all cars, trucks, and trailers wider than forty inches.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: What two clues tell you a headlight is aimed crookedly, and who should fix it?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: A crooked headlight wastes its beam and dazzles others, so night-vision trouble or constant oncoming flashes mean a mechanic should aim them.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: By how much can road grime cut your lamp brightness if you skip washing lenses?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Wash headlight, backup, brake, and tail lenses, since grime can slash their output by fifty percent.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Combine how you inspect exterior bulbs with the required lamp count on four-wheel vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Light checks happen outside the car, while the equipment counts demand two headlights, one red rear lamp, and a plate lamp.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Compare the rule for factory-installed blinkers against Iowa's width threshold requiring signals?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Any fitted signal must work, while signals become mandatory past forty inches of width.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Which headlight problem calls for a mechanic, and which one just needs soap and water?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Crooked beams need a mechanic re-aim, while dimmed lenses need only a wash.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: How should you maintain windshields regarding cracks, glare film, and winter washer reservoirs?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Swap out cracked or broken glass that shatters easily and clouds sight, keep the windshield clean against sun and headlight glare, and top up washer fluid with antifreeze wash when frost threatens.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: What winter clearing and wiper upkeep are required before pulling onto Iowa roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Scrape snow, ice, and frost off every window, and keep the mandatory wipers wiping well with fresh blades when they streak.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: How much light must pass through Iowa windshields and front side windows, and do medical waivers exist?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Iowa tint law lets the windshield and front side windows pass at least seventy percent of light, with no medical exemption granted.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: What two interior and glass clutter habits must you avoid to keep a clear view?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Guard a clear view by hanging nothing from the rearview mirror and pasting no decal clutter on the windshield.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How do you treat cracked auto glass differently from intact auto glass?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Broken glass gets replaced, while sound glass gets cleaned and washed with antifreeze fluid.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Pair your winter window-clearing duties with Iowa's front-glass tint requirement?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Wipers and snow clearing are driver chores, while the seventy-percent tint limit is the law with no medical pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: How do bald or unbalanced tires hurt safety and fuel economy, and what ride symptoms need a shop?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Worn, bald, or unbalanced tires stretch stopping distance, invite hydroplaning, wear faster, drink fuel, and fight steering and braking, while bouncing, wheel shake, or side-pull earns a mechanic visit.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: When should you gauge tire inflation, and where do you find the right pressure number?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Inflate tires to spec, gauging pressure cold against the driver-door sticker or owner manual.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: How do you use a penny to tell whether tire tread is worn past safe limits?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Probe tread with a head-first penny; tread short of Lincoln crown top marks an unsafe tire due for replacement.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: Contrast how you check tire air pressure with how you check tire tread depth?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Pressure gets gauged cold against the door sticker, while tread gets probed with a head-first penny.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: Distinguish what bald tread causes on wet roads from what bouncing or side-pulling indicates?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Bald tires stretch stops and invite slides, while bouncing and pulling send the car to a mechanic.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What should you do if your steering suddenly feels heavy, stiff, or slow to respond?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Steering gone stiff or slow to answer the wheel needs a mechanic inspection.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: What worn components are likely to blame if your car keeps bouncing up and down after a bump or stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Suspension steadies handling and comfort, so endless bouncing after bumps or stops signals worn shocks or parts.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Match sluggish wheel response and non-stop bouncing after dips to their underlying systems?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Stiff or lazy steering points at the steering gear, while endless bouncing points at shocks.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: What three jobs does the exhaust system perform, and why must you never idle inside a garage or sealed car?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Exhaust pipes away poison gas, muffles noise, and cools hot fumes, yet a leak can kill swiftly, so never idle in a garage or sit in a running car with every window shut.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Why is warming up an engine inside a garage forbidden?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: A leaky exhaust can kill in minutes, which is why idling in a garage is never allowed.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What road hazard and everyday costs come from an out-of-tune engine, and what guides its upkeep?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: A sour engine saps power, refuses starts, wastes fuel, fouls air, and may stall into traffic, so service it by the owner manual.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: For what sole purpose should you press your vehicle's horn?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: The horn is a life-saving warner reserved strictly for warning others.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: Pair how you maintain a rough engine with the single legitimate reason to sound your horn?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: A sour engine gets serviced by the manual, while the horn gets used for warnings only.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: How far behind must your center mirror show, and when are outside mirrors mandatory?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Your inside mirror must reveal two hundred feet astern; a load-blocked view demands an outside mirror, and vans must wear both outside mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: When must you adjust the driver's seat and mirrors to fit your frame?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Dial in seat and mirrors for your own body before every drive, since fit governs control.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: How far must your breastbone sit from the steering hub, and where should the wheel aim?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Sit spine-flat with at least ten inches of chest clearance from the wheel and the airbag aimed at your chest.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: How high should the top of the wheel sit, how does your right foot pivot, and how do shorter drivers keep ten inches?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Keep the wheel top at or below shoulder height, plant your heel to pivot between pedals, and let shorter drivers add a cushion or pedal extenders to hold the ten-inch gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: How high should you set your seat's head restraint behind your skull?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Float the head restraint level with the middle of your head.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: How should you posture and aim your inside rearview mirror?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Sit tall and frame the whole rear window in the inside mirror, your chief rearward eye.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: How do you lean and aim the left side mirror to minimize blind spots?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Tip your head to the left window and set the left mirror to just glimpse the car flank, a sliver that vanishes once you sit straight.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Where do you lean your head to set the passenger-side outside mirror?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Lean over the console and set the right mirror to just glimpse the right flank of the car.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: Pair the required sight distance of an inside mirror with the special mirror rule for vans?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: The rearview must show two hundred feet back, while vans must wear both outside mirrors regardless.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: Combine your minimum chest-to-wheel clearance with Iowa's blind-zone mirror adjustment method?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: The seat holds ten inches of chest clearance, while the mirrors get set by the lean-and-glimpse method.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Why must you still know how to drive unassisted even with modern safety features?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Assistance features like auto braking, blind-spot watch, and crash warnings raise safety only when used right within their limits, and you must still drive unassisted since tech can fail, need shutoff, or vanish in another car.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: How does Iowa's driving test separate safety helpers from convenience helpers?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Test day welcomes safety helpers such as backup cameras but bars convenience helpers such as adaptive cruise.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which camera, detection, speed, and lane warning systems may stay active during your driving test?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Permitted warning systems span backup alerts, blind-spot monitors, rear, sideview, and surround cameras, curve-speed warnings, bike, pedestrian, and obstacle detection, crash warnings, speed alerts, lane-departure warnings, parking sensors, and rear cross-traffic alerts.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Which four acting assists are allowed on test day, and which two convenience systems are banned?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.memory_hook: Four crash-assists in, two conveniences out
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Permitted assists cover auto emergency braking, auto reverse braking, lane keeping, and left-turn crash avoidance, while adaptive cruise and auto parallel parking stay banned.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Why does test day allow a backup camera while banning adaptive cruise control?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Test day welcomes safety helpers like backup cameras, while convenience helpers like adaptive cruise stay barred.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does the broad list of test-day warnings compare in count with approved acting assists?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: A long warning roster earns test-day approval, while only four acting assists join them.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Why does Iowa ban every convenience feature during the behind-the-wheel driving test?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Convenience features demand no testable skill, so none may run during the driving test.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What two resources should you use to master every new assistance feature on your vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Study the owner manual for every new feature and quiz the dealer on leftovers.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: How do convenience-feature bans on test day pair with owner-manual study beforehand?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Conveniences sit out test day entirely, while the owner manual stays required reading.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What do warning systems do when danger approaches, and who must execute the save?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Warning systems flash, beep, or buzz about looming crashes or faults yet stay mostly passive, leaving the save to you.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: In the partnership between warning systems and the human driver, who plays which role?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Warning systems stay passive announcers, while the driver stays the actor who prevents the crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Where do backup warnings scan, and which four checks must you still perform?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Backup warnings scan astern in reverse with sound or buzz, yet you still work side mirrors, rearview, head turns, and cameras.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: How do blind-spot monitors react when you signal toward a hidden car, and what checks remain?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Blind-spot monitors flag hidden alongside cars by symbol, sound, or buzz with extra scolding if you signal into them, yet lane changes still demand mirrors, head turns, and the monitor together.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How does the scanning zone of a backup warning differ from a blind-spot warning?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Backup warnings scan astern in reverse, while blind-spot warnings scan alongside for lane changes.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Where do rear cameras display a wide view in reverse, and what do they never replace?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Rear cameras paint a wide astern view on consoles, mirrors, or visors in reverse, yet never replace mirrors and head turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What triggers a sideview camera feed, when might it shut off, and what checks remain?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Sideview cameras stream the beside lane on signal or button, may stand in for mirrors, may sleep while backing or at speed, and still pair with mirrors and head turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Which four camera angles fuse into surround-view parking, and what checks still pair with it?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Surround-view fuses four wide cameras, nose, tail, left, and right, into a bird's-eye parking picture, yet still pairs with mirrors and head turns.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How do rear cameras and sideview cameras differ in trigger and direction?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Rear cameras show astern in reverse, while sideview cameras show alongside on signal.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: How does a sideview camera stream compare with a surround-view camera display?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Sideview streams one beside lane, while surround-view stitches four cameras into a parking bird's-eye.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Near what speed do pedestrian, cyclist, and obstacle alerts work, and why scan downtown yourself?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Detection alerts flag bikes, walkers, and obstacles at low speeds near twenty-five miles per hour, some only dead ahead and same-direction with a few auto-braking, yet never replace your own scanning, especially downtown.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: How do radar closing-gap chimes change rhythm as your bumper nears an obstacle?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Radar eyes fore, aft, or both judge closing gaps with beeps, flashes, buzzes, or brake pulses that quicken as you near, turning solid-toned when impact looms.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: How do curve-speed warnings know an upcoming bend is too sharp for your pace?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Curve-speed warnings track pace and place by GPS to scold hot curve and exit entries, yet you still carry a safe speed yourself.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What basic upkeep keeps radar and camera sensors able to detect anything at all?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Sensors must stay clean to sense at all.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: How do low-speed obstacle detection alerts differ from GPS curve-speed warnings?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Detection flags bikes, walkers, and obstacles at low speed, while curve warnings flag hot entries by GPS.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What do faster radar beeps tell you, and what makes warning sensors go silent?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Beeps quicken as gaps shrink, while dirty sensors silence every warning.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What do forward crash-warning systems do and NOT do when traffic slows ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Crash warnings flag slower or stopped obstacles ahead for timely braking or swerving without braking for you, while you keep distance and caution regardless.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How fast and far does forward crash warning scan, and how many seconds ahead across three speed bands?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: The system sweeps twenty times per second out to five hundred feet, granting about three seconds of warning at fifteen to eighteen miles per hour, four seconds at eighteen to fifty miles per hour, and five seconds past fifty miles per hour

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: What pedal action does forward crash warning skip despite sweeping five hundred feet twenty times per second?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Crash warnings never brake for you, while their sweeps reach five hundred feet twenty times a second.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: How should your foot respond when a GPS speeding alert chimes or flashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: With current GPS data the speeding alert beeps or flashes, calling for a gentle lift or light braking rather than a slam, yet you still watch your own speed and obey limits.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What road markings power lane-departure warnings, and do those warnings steer your car?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Lane-departure warnings buzz, flash, or beep drifting cars back toward center using painted lines, yet never hold your lane for you.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: What response fits a speeding alert, and what road cue powers a lane-departure warning?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: Speed alerts call for a gentle lift, while lane warnings lean on painted lines.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: What blind spots hamper parking sensors, and how do rear cross-traffic alerts help in lots?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Parking sensors beep faster as objects near with a solid tone at closest range yet miss flat, low, near, or far items, while cross-traffic alerts warn of crossing cars when backing; both still pair with mirrors, head turns, and cameras.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: How do targets differ between bumper parking sensors and rear cross-traffic alerts?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Parking sensors beep at still objects, while cross-traffic alerts warn of crossing cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: How do assist systems step beyond passive warning systems, and why stay ready?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Assist systems shoulder part of driving, braking or steering with or for you, though you may still need to act.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: What single line separates passive warning systems from active assist systems?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Warning systems only announce, while assist systems brake or steer with you.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: When does automatic emergency braking step in, and what habits remain yours?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Auto emergency braking senses dawdling or halted traffic and objects ahead, braking hard when you fail to, while you keep scanning and spacing.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What two-stage sequence does automatic reverse braking run when an obstacle blocks your tail?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: Auto reverse braking beeps or flashes at rear obstacles while backing, then brakes itself if you ignore it, yet still pairs with mirrors, head turns, and cameras.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: How does lane-keeping assist work, and what three line conditions make it quit?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Lane keeping alerts drifting cars, then nudges the wheel home unless you override, but quits on faint, snowy, or dirty lines and never excuses your own control.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: How does left-turn crash avoidance intervene if you start turning across oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Left-turn avoidance watches oncoming traffic on slow lefts, sounding and braking and even freezing forward motion when gaps run short, yet you still judge the turn yourself.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: How does automatic reverse braking's intervention differ from lane-keeping assist's intervention?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: Reverse braking halts the car for rear obstacles, while lane keeping nudges it home between lines.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: What road surface defeats lane-keeping assist, and what mistake triggers left-turn avoidance?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.memory_hook: Faint stripes quit, short lefts freeze
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: Lane keeping quits on faint paint, while left-turn avoidance freezes short gaps at slow lefts.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: What does adaptive cruise control manage in traffic, and when should you rest it?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Adaptive cruise holds your chosen short, medium, or long gap, slowing and even stopping and restarting in jams, yet demands your attention and rests in bad weather.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: How do car and driver split duties during automatic parallel parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Auto parallel parking finds the slot and talks you through pulling ahead, reversing, and releasing the wheel, while you brake, watch, and finish the alignment.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: How do adaptive cruise control and automatic parallel parking split work with the driver?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: Adaptive cruise holds a following gap you set, while auto parking finds a slot you brake into.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: How strictly does Iowa enforce and punish alcohol- or drug-impaired driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Impaired driving ranks among the hardest-enforced road laws, and Iowa punishes alcohol and drug intoxication steeply.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: What blood-alcohol level or drug presence defines Operating While Intoxicated, and which three samples prove it?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Operating while intoxicated means a BAC of point zero eight or higher or any controlled substance aboard, proven by breath, urine, or blood tests.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How does Iowa's enforcement priority pair with the two-part legal trigger for OWI?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Impaired driving draws top enforcement priority, while OWI itself means point zero eight BAC or any controlled substance.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: How many days of driving privileges can you still lose despite a criminal-court acquittal?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Even a criminal-court acquittal still costs at least one hundred eighty days of driving privileges, and repeat offenses stretch revocations and sharpen criminal pain.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Why does winning in criminal court fail to save privileges, and what do repeat OWI arrests do?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Acquittal still costs one hundred eighty days of privileges, while repeats stretch revocations further.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: What sobriety-check agreement comes built into holding an Iowa license or driving through as a visitor?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Holding an Iowa license signs you to field sobriety tests on officer demand under Iowa Code section 321J point six, binding visitors too.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Does refusing a breathalyzer save you, and what revocation and minimum fine hit automatically?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Refusing the breathalyzer neither blocks conviction nor saves your license, and out-punishes failing with an automatic one-year revocation plus a minimum one thousand two hundred fifty dollars fine.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Which two extra requirements can follow a breathalyzer-refusal conviction in Iowa?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Refusal convictions may add a mandatory substance-use class and evaluation or a self-paid ignition interlock.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Who falls under Iowa implied consent, and how does refusing compare with failing?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Licenses pre-consent to sobriety tests for residents and visitors, while refusal out-punishes failing with a year off plus one thousand two hundred fifty dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: At what blood-alcohol level do underage drivers hit OWI, and how long are the two revocation tiers?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Underage drivers hit OWI at point zero two BAC, losing privileges at least sixty days, or at least one hundred eighty days past point zero eight.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: Can an offender under age eighteen obtain a temporary restricted license during an OWI revocation?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Offenders under eighteen get no temporary restricted license during an OWI revocation.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: How does an underage driver's revocation jump between point-zero-two and point-zero-eight BAC?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Underage OWI starts at point zero two with sixty-day revocations, while adult-level point zero eight stretches them to one hundred eighty days.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Where may an open alcohol container legally ride, and what fine hits cabin violations?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Open alcohol belongs to no cabin occupant, though trunks may carry it, and cabin violations cost each driver and rider up to a two hundred dollars simple misdemeanor.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How does Iowa treat open alcohol inside the passenger cabin compared with the trunk?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Cabin open containers fine every occupant two hundred dollars, while trunk transport stays lawful.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: In what four dangerous ways does drowsy driving mirror drunk driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Drowsy driving kills like drunk driving through slow reactions, lane weaving, road departures, and crash proneness.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Which five mental or physical warning signs show drowsiness creeping in?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Mind warnings of drowsiness include daydreaming, forgotten miles, repeated yawns, eye rubbing, and a drooping head.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Which five driving behaviors signal road drowsiness, and what three fixes answer them?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Road warnings of drowsiness include lane drifting, tailgating, rumble-strip strikes, restlessness, and irritability, all cueing a break, a safe pullover, or a driver swap.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What blood-alcohol level matches the impairment of staying awake eighteen straight hours?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Eighteen straight waking hours impair like a zero point zero eight percent BAC with matching crash risk.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How deadly is drowsy driving, and which early mental clues warn you first?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Drowsiness kills like drunkenness, while its mind warnings span daydreams, yawns, and drooping heads.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How do lane-drift and rumble-strip warnings pair with Iowa's eighteen-waking-hour benchmark?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Road warnings span drifting, tailgating, and rumble strips, while eighteen waking hours match zero point zero eight impairment.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Which three road-blocking surprises should you plan around before every short or long trip?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Plan every trip, familiar or far, around weather, construction, and crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Which state website and mobile app report live Iowa highway and interstate conditions?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Iowa five hundred eleven serves highway and interstate conditions at 511ia.org and through its free mobile app.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How do weather, construction, and crash checks pair with Iowa's five-one-one tools?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Weather, work zones, and crashes shape every trip plan, while Iowa five hundred eleven reports them online and in-app.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: How do core driving fundamentals apply once you move from basic streets to complex roads, weather, and emergencies?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: This chapter ports basics into live scenarios from odd roads to weather and emergencies.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: Which everyday driveways, lots, and road junctions all count as intersections?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Intersections span every merge or crossing: cross streets, side streets, drives, lots, and public roads.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: Walk through the three ordered looks for approaching and entering an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Work crossings in three looks: read type and controls ahead, scan for a clear path, then sweep left-right-left for cars and walkers while assuming no gifts of space.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Why must you wait until an approaching vehicle actually begins turning instead of trusting its turn signal?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Distrust strangers' blinkers, since they may overshoot your turn or stick on, especially unsticking motorcycle lamps; move only once they truly swing.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: Combine what counts as an intersection with the three-step visual scan used at each one?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Every merge counts as an intersection, while three ordered looks work each one.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: How do assuming zero courtesy and distrusting lit turn signals protect you at corners?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Triple looks assume no courtesy, while lit blinkers earn no trust until cars swing.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: How do you cross a four-lane divided rural highway in two stages using the median?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: Split rural four-lane crossings at the median: halt at the sign, take the median on a left-side gap, wait there, then finish on a right-side gap.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: What two hazards arise from high rural speeds and narrow highway medians when long vehicles cross?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: Such roads run fast and demand focus, and long rigs may overhang skinny medians.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: How does two-gap median crossing pair with watching median width for long rigs?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: Wide rural crossings split at medians in two gap judgments, while fast traffic and long rigs punish rushing.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: How do the entrance, acceleration, and merge zones of a highway on-ramp work, and what do through drivers do?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: On-ramps run entrance scan, acceleration and merge at traffic speed without stopping short of need, then joined travel where incumbents slide to admit you.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: How do entering ramp drivers and current highway drivers share a smooth merge?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: Ramp entrants scan, accelerate, and merge unstopped, while incumbents slide to admit them.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: How does a reduced-conflict intersection replace a direct side-road left turn across four lanes?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Reduced-conflict crossings turn side-road lefts into rights, then left-lane merges and U-turns at median gaps, facing one direction at a time with no two-way gap wait.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: What dangerous two-way wait disappears at a reduced-conflict J-turn intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: Reduced-conflict lefts become rights plus U-turns, while one-direction focus drops the double-gap wait.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: What unusual lane shift happens inside a diverging diamond interchange, and what traffic benefit does it create?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: Diverging diamonds briefly drive the wrong side to unsnarl two busy roads with shorter signal waits.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Why does a diverging diamond route traffic briefly to the opposite side of the overpass?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: Diamonds detour briefly wrong-sided, while shorter signals pay for the strangeness.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: Which direction does traffic circle inside a roundabout, and what controls entry instead of stoplights?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: Roundabouts circle counterclockwise signalless around islands under yield guidance at calming speeds.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What two yields happen in sequence as you enter a single-lane roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: Single-lane drivers approach at advisory pace yielding to crosswalk users, then yield at the line to circle traffic and join gaps counterclockwise.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: How do you drive inside a single-lane roundabout and exit cleanly?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: Ride through without stopping, then signal and peel right, again yielding to crosswalk users.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: How do pedestrians cross a roundabout leg safely using the raised splitter island?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.memory_hook: Look left, pause island, look right
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Walkers look left, cross to the splitter island, look right, and finish across.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: What two options do cyclists have for navigating a roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: Cyclists generally walk bikes as pedestrians, though veterans may ride motorist-style mid-lane off the curb while yielding to crosswalks.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: Why do roundabouts keep moving without stop signs, and who holds priority over entering cars?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: Rings yield rather than stop at calming speeds, while entries yield to circle traffic and crosswalks.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: Summarize how cars exit, pedestrians cross, and cyclists ride or walk at single-lane roundabouts?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.memory_hook: Blink right, use islands, claim center
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: Single-lane rings ride through to signaled right exits, while walkers island-hop and riders walk or center up.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: What four habits are essential when approaching and exiting a multi-lane roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.memory_hook: Pick lane early, yield both, blink
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: Multi-lane rings demand pre-picked lanes per signs, full yield on entry, right signals past the pre-exit street, and cross-lane awareness.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: What three mistakes are forbidden once you are inside a multi-lane roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Inside rings forbid lane swaps, truck shadowing against straddles and blind eyes, and overrunning the outside lane past its limit.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: Where must pedestrians never walk at a roundabout, and why do raised truck aprons ring the center island?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.memory_hook: Skip center island, aprons serve trailers
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Never stroll circulating lanes to the island, and cede aprons to long trailers' rear wheels.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: Combine what you must do before entering a multi-lane roundabout with what you must never do inside?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: Multi-lane rings pre-pick lanes and signal late rights, while swaps, truck shadows, and outside overruns stay banned.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: How does loose gravel change tire grip, and what four adjustments keep control?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Loose gravel steals grip, so slow down, shun sharp wheel, ease pedals, and stretch gaps.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: Which five rural obstacles block intersection and driveway sightlines in farm country?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: Trees, corn, buildings, hills, and dust blind rural sightlines, so map blind spots early.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: How do you approach an unsigned rural gravel intersection, and which vehicle yields?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: Unsigned gravel crossings want caution, low speed, and stop readiness with no faith in dust clouds; left-side cars yield and nobody assumes anything.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: What happens if tires drop onto a soft rural shoulder, and how should you pass oncoming vehicles there?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: Soft rural shoulders suck cars ditchward, so creep near shoulders and past oncoming wheels.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: Which headlight setting helps other drivers see you through thick gravel dust?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: Burn low beams through heavy dust to be seen.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: Why are rural gravel roads a double hazard of traction and sightlines?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: Gravel steals grip and sight together, while gentle inputs and mapped blind spots answer.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: Tie together Iowa's unsigned-gravel yield rule, soft-shoulder hazard, and dust headlight rule?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.memory_hook: Yield right, respect shoulders, low beams
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: Unsigned gravel corners yield leftward with zero assumptions, while soft shoulders and dust demand creeping and low beams.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: What five kinds of roadway info do traffic signs share, and how do shape and color help you?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Traffic signs tell you the laws, hazards, places, directions, and services around you, and each sign's shape and color hint at what kind it is.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What three types of driver action does the color red command on a roadway sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Red means stop, yield, or obey whatever the sign shows.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: What navigation details does a green background provide on highway signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Green gives direction, naming a place or how far away it lies.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Which roadside traveler needs and destinations are marked by blue traffic signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Blue points travelers to services such as rest areas, hospitals, lodging, fuel, food, and attractions.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: What kind of destinations do brown roadway signs guide drivers toward?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Brown guides you to recreation and cultural points of interest such as parks and historic sites.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: What message category does a standard yellow background communicate on a road sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: A yellow traffic sign gives a general warning.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Which three vulnerable crossing zones use fluorescent yellow-green warning signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Fluorescent yellow-green marks pedestrian, bicycle, and school warning signs.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What legal weight does a white background carry on a traffic sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: White carries regulatory messages about enforceable laws and ordinances.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: How do red signs and white signs split the job of regulating drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Red commands an action such as stop or yield, while white states the enforceable rule behind such commands.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How do green, blue, and brown guide signs divide directions, services, and destinations?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.memory_hook: Green routes, blue services, brown parks
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Green points the way and blue points to services, while brown points only to recreation and cultural sites.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What roadway situation does an orange sign announce, and what two hazards must you watch for?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Orange warns of road work and temporary traffic control, so watch for changing speed limits and workers on the road.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which emergency roadside situations are marked by fluorescent pink warning and guide signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Fluorescent pink marks incident-management warnings and guides for crash cleanup, debris removal, and traffic control.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: What separates a plain yellow warning sign from a fluorescent yellow-green sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: Plain yellow warns of general hazards, while fluorescent yellow-green is reserved for pedestrian, bicycle, and school warnings.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How does the hazard marked by an orange sign differ from the hazard on a yellow sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Orange marks temporary work-zone conditions, while yellow marks general warnings with no work-zone tie.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: How do fluorescent pink signs and orange signs divide temporary roadside hazards?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Fluorescent pink covers incident response such as crash cleanup and debris removal, while orange covers road work and maintenance.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which single traffic sign owns the eight-sided octagon shape, and what action does it require?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: The eight-sided octagon belongs to the stop sign alone, and you must come to a full stop where it controls the intersection.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What right-of-way duty does an equilateral triangle-shaped sign place on a driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: The triangle-shaped sign means you must yield the right of way.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which three broad sign categories can appear on a rectangular panel?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Rectangles serve as regulatory, guide, and warning signs.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: How does the driver action required at an octagonal sign differ from an equilateral triangular sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: An octagonal stop sign requires a complete halt at the intersection it controls; an equilateral triangular sign requires drivers to give the right of way.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: On which side of the roadway is a pennant sign mounted, and what does it forbid ahead?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: The pennant hangs on the left side of the road and warns you that passing is prohibited ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn drivers about, and how should you respond?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: The diamond warns of special road hazards, and its words or pictures tell you why to slow down or take extra care.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: What specific hazard ahead is announced by a circular traffic sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: A circular sign tells you a railroad crossing lies ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Which two school-related zones are marked by a five-sided pentagon sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: The five-sided pentagon marks school areas and school crossings.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Where do crossbuck signs stand, and what does the number plaque underneath tell you?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Crossbuck signs stand at each railroad crossing, and the number plate beneath them tells how many sets of tracks you must cross.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: How do the circular railroad sign and the X-shaped crossbuck divide warning locations?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: The circle warns that a railroad crossing lies ahead, while the crossbuck stands at the crossing itself.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: How does a left-side pennant sign differ in purpose from a diamond-shaped sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: A pennant sign appears beside the left edge of the road to warn that passing is prohibited. A diamond sign warns about particular roadway hazards.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: How does the range of messages on a rectangle compare with what a diamond sign carries?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: The rectangle can carry regulatory, guide, or warning messages, while the diamond carries warnings only.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: What rules do regulatory signs cover, and what does a red circle with a slash forbid?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Regulatory signs state the rules for direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking, and a red circle with a slash over a symbol always prohibits something such as a left turn, right turn, or U-turn.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What two speed bounds can speed limit signs post, and what road conditions does the maximum assume?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Speed limit signs post the fastest or slowest safe speed allowed, with the maximum written for ideal driving conditions.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: How should you adjust for rain, snow, or fog, and what if a posted minimum exceeds your pace?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Drop below the posted maximum when rain, snow, or fog makes the road slippery or hard to see, and take a different route when a posted minimum is too fast for you.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How does a posted maximum speed limit differ from a posted minimum speed limit in driver action?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: A posted maximum assumes ideal conditions and invites you to go slower when grip or sight fails, while a posted minimum is a floor that should send too-slow drivers to another route.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: How do lane control signs and matching pavement arrows tell you where your lane may travel?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Lane control signs show where you may go or turn, using arrow symbols on roadside or overhead signs and sometimes white arrows painted on the pavement.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Where does a no-passing zone begin, and what determines whether passing is allowed outside it?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: No-passing signs mark stretches where passing is unsafe, starting at the zone sign itself, with passing areas set by sight distance and passing allowed only when safe; the matching pavement markings are detailed on handbook page forty-five.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: What separates the job of lane control signs from the job of no-passing signs?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Lane control signs tell you where you may go or turn, while no-passing signs tell you where passing is unsafe.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Where must you halt first at a stop sign, and how do you move forward if visibility requires edging?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: A stop sign orders a full stop until crossing traffic and the crosswalk clear, halting first at any stop line and then edging to the sign or intersection edge before proceeding when safe.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What two actions does a yield sign require as you enter an intersection or roadway?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: A yield sign orders you to slow down and give the right of way to traffic in the intersection or road you are entering.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How do the stopping and right-of-way rules at a stop sign differ from those at a yield sign?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.memory_hook: Stop halts every time, yield slows
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: At a stop sign, halt completely and wait for crossing traffic and the crosswalk to clear. Use an available stop line; if needed, advance afterward to the sign or intersection edge, then proceed when safe. At a yield sign, reduce speed and give priority to traffic in the intersection or road you are entering.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: What traffic rule does a one-way regulatory sign enforce?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: A one-way sign means traffic flows only in the direction of its arrow.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: What roadway layout does a divided-highway regulatory sign announce, and how must you steer?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: The divided-highway sign means the road ahead splits, so steer around the island or barrier.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How does a one-way sign differ from a divided-highway regulatory sign?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: The one-way sign channels traffic along its arrow, while the divided-highway sign announces a split ahead with an island or barrier to drive around.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Which three types of roadway openings are guarded by do-not-enter signs?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Do-not-enter signs mark openings you must not use, such as exit ramps, divided-road crossovers, and one-way stretches.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: What three emergency actions must you take immediately upon spotting a wrong-way sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: A wrong-way sign means you turned into opposing traffic, so leave the traveled roadway, stop, and turn around as quickly and safely as you can.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How does a do-not-enter sign differ in timing and meaning from a wrong-way sign?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Do-not-enter signs forbid you from going in, while the wrong-way sign tells you the mistake already happened and orders an escape off the traveled road.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Where is the blue rail emergency notification sign posted, and what two details does it give callers?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: The blue emergency notification sign stands on both sides of every rail crossing with a railroad phone number and crossing ID for reporting stalled vehicles, broken signals, or any track hazard.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: How does the blue rail-crossing notification sign differ from stop and yield signs?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: The blue rail-crossing sign summons railroad help by phone with a crossing ID, while stop and yield signs command intersection behavior.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What colors and usual shape identify warning signs, and what two preparations do they demand?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols and mostly diamond-shaped, telling you to slow down and stand ready to stop for a hazard ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What hazard ahead does an intersection or crossroad warning sign alert you to watch for?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: An intersection or crossroad sign means another road crosses yours ahead, so watch carefully for traffic crossing your path.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: Why is a signal-ahead warning sign placed along faster highways and approaches?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: A signal-ahead sign on a faster road tells you to expect an intersection with a stoplight.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: What does a merging-traffic warning sign tell drivers already traveling on the main roadway?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: A merging-traffic sign tells drivers on the main road to expect other vehicles blending into their lane.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: How does a signal-ahead warning sign differ from a merging-traffic warning sign?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: Signal-ahead promises a stoplight at an upcoming intersection, while merging-traffic warns that other vehicles will blend into your lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: What road transition does a two-way-traffic warning sign announce, and where must you position your car?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: A two-way-traffic sign means you are leaving a one-way road for a two-way road, so keep to the right.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: What change in roadway layout does a divided-highway-begins warning sign announce?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: A divided-highway-begins sign means two-way traffic is about to split around a center strip.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: What hazard returns when you pass a divided-highway-ends warning sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: A divided-highway-ends sign means the center strip is ending, so watch for oncoming vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: How do the divided-highway-begins and divided-highway-ends warning signs point to opposite changes?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Divided-begins warns that two-way traffic is about to split, while divided-ends warns that the split is over and oncoming traffic returns.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: What does a T-intersection-ahead warning sign tell you about your current road?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: A T-intersection-ahead sign means your road ends, so get ready to turn left or right.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How does a crossroad warning sign differ from a T-intersection warning sign?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: A crossroad sign means another road crosses your continuing road, while a T-intersection sign means your road ends entirely.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: What happens at a lane-ends warning sign, and which lane of drivers must yield?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: A lane-ends sign means two lanes are merging into one, with merging traffic yielding.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: What roadway alignment does a gradual-curve warning sign announce ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: A gradual-curve sign means the road bends gently ahead, so prepare for the direction change.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: Why do highway crews place yellow chevron alignment signs along the outside of a curve?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: Chevron signs back up curve signs wherever a direction change needs extra emphasis.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: How do a gradual-curve diamond and roadside chevron signs work differently on bends?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: The gradual-curve sign announces a gentle bend, while chevrons reinforce a curve that needs extra emphasis.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: What surface hazard does a slippery-when-wet warning sign identify, and when must you slow?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: A slippery-when-wet sign means the pavement ahead slicks over in rain, so slow down in wet weather.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: Who does a hill warning sign apply to, and what check should you make before descending?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: A hill sign warns every vehicle that the road drops ahead, so test your brakes before the descent.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: What does the number on a yellow ramp-speed warning sign tell exiting drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: A ramp-speed sign posts the recommended speed for an exit ramp.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: How should you adjust your driving when you pass a deer-crossing warning sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: A deer-crossing sign means deer may step onto the road nearby, so slow down and scan carefully.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: What slow road user does a horse-drawn-vehicle sign warn of, and how should you pass?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: A horse-drawn-vehicle sign means slow-moving buggies may share the road, so cut your speed and pass gently.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What should you expect and do after passing a farm-machinery warning sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: A farm-machinery sign means slow equipment may share the road, so cut your speed and pass gently.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: What do the horse-drawn-vehicle and farm-machinery signs share in driver action, and what differs?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: Horse-drawn vehicles and farm machinery draw the same response of slower speed and a gentle pass, differing only in what kind of slow mover to expect.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Besides people walking on foot, whom must you watch for at an Iowa pedestrian-crossing warning sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: A pedestrian-crossing sign means watching for everyone crossing on foot or wheels, including wheelchairs and low-speed micromobility devices, with details in the pedestrian-conveyance section covered later.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: What activity ahead does a school-bus-stop-ahead warning sign prepare you to encounter?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: A school-bus-stop-ahead sign means a bus will soon load or unload children nearby, so watch for children and stand ready to stop.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: What distinguishes a school-bus-stop-ahead sign from an advance-school-crossing sign?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: School-bus-stop-ahead warns of children boarding a bus, while advance-school-crossing warns of a marked crossing near a school.
