sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Under Iowa's twenty twenty-four crosswalk law, which two groups hold right-of-way inside crosswalks?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: A twenty twenty-four Iowa law orders drivers to yield crosswalk right-of-way to people on foot and to riders of any human-powered device, called a pedestrian conveyance.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: How does Iowa define a pedestrian conveyance, and which five everyday examples does the manual name?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: A conveyance is any human-powered device used to get around without walking or to move another person, including wheelchairs, strollers, skateboards, scooters, and electric personal assistive mobility devices.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Whenever the Iowa manual uses the word pedestrian, which road users are included?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Every use of the word pedestrian in the manual covers both walkers and conveyance riders.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: Do walkers on foot have stronger crosswalk right-of-way than riders on human-powered conveyances?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Walkers and conveyance riders share identical crosswalk rights, since the manual folds every human-powered device into its pedestrian term.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: How does Iowa classify skateboards and scooters at crosswalks, and what must drivers do?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: Skateboards and scooters are examples of human-powered pedestrian conveyances. Drivers must give people using these devices the right of way.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: What top speed and vehicle types are marked by a reflective orange triangle on the rear?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle's rear means it travels at thirty-five miles per hour or less, as seen on maintenance rigs, farm vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What do highway guide signs and green mile markers each help drivers calculate or report?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Guide signs give directions and distances to cities, airports, borders, parks, and museums, while mile markers count miles from the state line for exit math and emergency location.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Which four roadside traveler facilities does the manual highlight on service signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Service signs point to rest areas, fuel, campgrounds, and hospitals.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: How do guide signs, service signs, and route shields divide highway navigation duties?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Guide signs name places and distances, service signs name traveler comforts, and route signs name the road itself by shape.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Which three authorized people can direct roadway traffic that drivers are legally required to obey?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Officers, highway workers, and school crossing guards may direct traffic, and you must follow their directions.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: How does a solid red traffic light differ in procedure from a flashing red light?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Solid red orders a complete stop, while flashing red is handled exactly like a stop sign.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: How should you respond when a traffic signal turns solid yellow ahead of you?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: On solid yellow, hold back when you can stop safely and otherwise clear the intersection with care.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal allow, and whom must you yield to?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Flashing yellow means advance with caution, yielding to vehicles and pedestrians until the way is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Why does a solid green light never give you permission to launch blindly into an intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Solid green means go only when the way is clear, yielding to anyone still inside and letting trapped traffic clear after the change.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: What separates what solid red orders for through lanes from what flashing red creates?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Solid red orders a full stop for through traffic, while flashing red turns the signal into a stop sign for every approach.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does the decision on a solid yellow light differ from a flashing yellow light?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Solid yellow asks whether you can stop, demanding a hold when possible, while flashing yellow grants passage conditioned only on caution and yielding.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: What must drivers in a turn lane do when facing a steady red arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: A steady red arrow forces turning drivers to stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: What does a steady yellow arrow warn turning drivers, and who may complete the turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow warns the turn signal is going red, so hold back when stoppable and finish the turn only from inside the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Why must you yield before turning left on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, since the opposing lanes hold green.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: What movement does a steady green arrow grant, what path does it forbid, and what duty remains?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: A steady green arrow permits the indicated turn while oncoming traffic waits, yet forbids going straight and still requires giving way to anyone already inside.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How do a steady red arrow and a flashing yellow arrow differ for left-turning traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: The steady red arrow forbids the turn outright, while the flashing yellow arrow permits a left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does a steady yellow arrow differ in meaning from a steady green arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: The steady yellow arrow warns a protected turn is ending, while the steady green arrow grants the turn but never the straight path.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: Why must drivers never stop on railroad tracks, and what warns you before reaching them?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Treat every rail crossing with extra care and never halt on the tracks, since trains cannot brake fast and advance signs plus pavement markings announce the rails ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Which three inside-the-car steps help you hear and spot a train as you approach tracks?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Near the tracks, drop distractions, roll the windows down, and silence the music so you can sense a train.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What two details posted at every crossing let you report stalls, signal faults, or track damage?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Each crossing posts its railroad name with an emergency number to call for signal faults, stalls, obstructions, or track damage.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What do flashing crossing lights or lowered gates mean, and what move is strictly illegal?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: At gated or lighted crossings, flashing lights or lowered gates mean a train is coming, so obey them and never cross or weave around a gate.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Which signs mark a passive railroad crossing, and how must you approach one?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Passive crossings show only a crossbuck with a stop or yield sign, so slow down, look for the train, and always expect one.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: How do active railroad crossings and passive railroad crossings differ in equipment and driver duty?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Active crossings command obedience to lights and gates, while passive crossings offer only a crossbuck with a stop or yield sign and demand a visual check.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Where are you allowed to drive across railroad tracks, and what is true about ungated rails?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Cross tracks only at marked crossings, heed every sign and signal, and remember that ungated tracks still carry trains announced by advance signs and markings.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: Why are rail cars fitted with reflective side stripes, and what should you scan for at night?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: Rail cars wear reflective stripes for night and murky weather, so scan for the train itself before rolling across.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: Why do drivers misjudge approaching trains, and what does a multi-track crossing warn about?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: Always expect a train, which may run closer and faster than it looks on any track at any time, with extra tracks meaning extra trains, so confirm a clear view both ways first and never try to beat one.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: How far back from the nearest rail must waiting cars stop, and what gear mistake is banned on tracks?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Cross only when sure of clearing fully, since trains overhang the rails; when waiting, keep fifteen feet between your vehicle and the closest rail, and never shift gears mid-crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: How does the fifteen-foot rail rule differ from the fifteen-to-fifty-foot stopping band?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: The fifteen-foot waiting gap keeps a stopped car clear of the nearest rail, while the fifteen-to-fifty band marks where buses and hazmat must halt before crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: Which rail-safety organization is credited for the illustrated sign-and-signal guide in the Iowa manual?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: The page after the rail-crossing rules holds an illustrated guide to rail signs and signals credited to Operation Lifesaver.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which four vehicle groups must stop fifteen to fifty feet before tracks, and what excuses that stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: School and charter buses, hired-ride drivers, and placarded hazmat haulers must halt fifteen to fifty feet before the rails, then cross; an officer's or signal's order to proceed and a posted EXEMPT sign both excuse the stop.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Under what three specific conditions may buses, paying-passenger rides, and hazmat rigs cross rails without stopping?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Before crossing railway tracks, school buses, charter buses, drivers transporting paying passengers and vehicles required to display hazardous-material placards must halt fifteen to fifty feet from the tracks. This stop is unnecessary when a police officer or highway traffic signal directs traffic onward, or when an EXEMPT sign marks the crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: If your car stalls on the rails with a train approaching, what escape path protects you from flying wreckage?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Stalled on the tracks with a train near, keep cranking the starter until the train shows, stand clear waving at the engineer, then get everyone out at once and walk clear of the rails at a forty-five-degree angle toward the oncoming train.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: If your vehicle gets stuck on a crossing with no train visible, what exact sequence should you follow?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Stuck or stalled at a crossing, empty the vehicle and run far even with no train in sight, then phone the blue-and-white ENS sign's number with its crossing ID, or call emergency services at nine-one-one when no sign stands.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: How does the manual's response to a track stall with a train visible differ from one with empty tracks?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: A stall with a train in view adds restart attempts and engineer-waving to the evacuation, while a stall with no train in view goes straight to evacuation plus the ENS call.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: Which four traffic-control tools appear in work zones, and what shape are most orange signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Work zones add arrow boards, temporary signals, flaggers, and channelizing hardware, with mostly diamond-shaped orange signs and only a few rectangles.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: Which four types of road crews use work-zone setups, and what happens to traffic fines inside them?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Those devices mark construction, maintenance, survey, and utility work, steering drivers and walkers past the crew; stay sharp because fines may double there.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: What four driving habits keep you safe while traveling through an active work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: In work zones, match speed to conditions, obey every sign, signal, and flagger, stretch your following gap, and lock your full attention on driving.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: What lane change or hazard does a large flashing arrow panel usually announce ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: Big flashing arrow panels usually signal a closed lane or shoulder.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: What high-visibility colors do work-zone flaggers wear, and what primary tool directs traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Flaggers with stop-or-slow paddles direct work traffic and must be obeyed; they wear fluorescent yellow-green or orange and mostly use paddle signs, with red flags only at times.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: What job do barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones, and tube markers perform in a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: Barricades, upright panels, drums, cones, and tube markers warn of odd or risky layouts and funnel drivers safely through.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: How do arrow boards, channelizing hardware, and flaggers divide traffic control inside a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.memory_hook: Boards close, cones steer, flaggers command
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Arrow boards announce closures, channelizing hardware steers the path, and flaggers direct traffic with paddles that must be obeyed.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: How much legal authority do pavement markings carry compared with upright road signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Pavement markings steer and regulate traffic like signs do, appearing alone or beside signs and signals.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: How do white lane stripes and yellow lane stripes differ in traffic direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: White lines divide lanes flowing the same way, while yellow lines divide opposing traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: Which paint color separates drivers traveling together, and which separates drivers coming toward each other?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: White paint separates traffic flowing together, while yellow paint separates traffic flowing against each other.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: When a solid yellow stripe sits next to a broken yellow stripe, which lane can legally pass?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Where a solid yellow line runs beside a dashed one, the solid side may not pass while the dashed side may pass when safe.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does your passing privilege change depending on whether the solid or broken yellow stripe touches your lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Beside a solid yellow line you must hold your lane, while beside its dashed twin you may pass when safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What pavement shape forms a yield line, and which three roadside signs pair with it?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Yield lines use white, solid triangular markings aimed at approaching traffic. They identify the yielding point for three signs: Yield Here to Pedestrians and Bicycles, Yield, and Yield Here To Pedestrians.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Where must your front bumper halt for a stop sign or red signal, and who gets priority?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: When a sign or signal demands a stop, halt ahead of the stop line or the crosswalk, and give way to anyone inside or stepping into the crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How does the job of a painted stop line differ from the job of a crosswalk?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: The stop line fixes where your vehicle must halt, while the crosswalk fixes where pedestrians cross and must be yielded to.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Why must you scan for people on foot even at intersections with zero painted crosswalk bars?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Not every crosswalk is painted, so stay alert for pedestrians at intersections with no marked crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does your duty toward pedestrians compare at striped crosswalks versus bare unmarked corners?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Painted crosswalks define the crossing zone, yet unpainted crossings carry the same pedestrian alert duty.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What do large white arrows painted inside a travel lane tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Painted lane arrows dictate which moves a lane allows or requires.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What marks a reversible lane on the pavement, and how do you verify you may enter it?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Reversible lanes flip direction by time of day, usually between double-dashed yellow lines, so confirm the lane is yours from roadside signs, overhead signs, or special lights before entering.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: Above a reversible lane, what does each overhead signal mean from green arrow to red and yellow Xs?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Over a reversible lane, a green arrow opens the lane below it, a red X closes it, a flashing yellow X limits it to turns, and a steady yellow X orders you out as soon as safety allows.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How do the four overhead reversible-lane signals split open, closed, turning, and vacating commands?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Green opens the reversible lane and red closes it, while flashing yellow narrows it to turns and steady yellow evicts you.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: How is a shared center left-turn lane marked, what is allowed inside it, and what move is banned?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: The shared left-turn lane serves left turns from both directions with alternating arrow markings between solid-and-dashed yellow borders; you may enter and wait there but never use it to pass.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What pavement or sign shape marks a reserved lane, and who may drive in it?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Reserved lanes belong to special vehicles by posted signs, often with a white diamond at the roadside or on the pavement; stay out unless you drive a qualifying vehicle, and the handbook's example reserves one for high-occupancy vehicles with two or more aboard.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How does access to a shared center left-turn lane contrast with a white-diamond reserved lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: The shared left-turn lane welcomes left turns from both directions with waiting allowed, while a reserved lane admits only its posted vehicle class.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Which lane is meant for passing on multi-lane roads, and where should you cruise across three or more lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: On multi-lane roads the left lane generally serves passing; with three or more same-direction lanes, cruise in the right or center except to pass, favoring the center when merging traffic is heavy.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: May you drive or overtake on a paved or gravel shoulder without official direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Never drive or pass on the shoulder, paved or not, unless a device or official sends you there; other drivers will not expect you and may pull over blindly.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How does Iowa law contrast using the left lane on a multi-lane road against using any shoulder?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: With at least two lanes moving the same way, the left lane is usually for passing. Driving on the shoulder is prohibited unless a traffic-control device or official instructs you to do it. Passing on any shoulder is prohibited, paved or unpaved.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: On a three-lane highway, how do the left lane and center lane split passing and ramp-merging duties?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: The left lane serves passing while the center lane serves heavy merging traffic, with cruising otherwise kept right or center.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Where no lane arrows are painted, which lane starts your turn, which lane finishes it, and when may you change lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: With no turn markings, start from the lane nearest your turn side and finish in the lane nearest your origin, moving directly without crossing lines or blocking traffic, and shift lanes only after the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: What lines, icons, and physical separators mark a dedicated bike lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Bike lanes are roadway slices for cyclists marked by solid white lines with bike symbols and signs, sometimes further split off by double white lines, curbs, posts, or planters.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What two rules apply wherever a bike lane is painted bright green?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Where a bike lane runs green, scan for cyclists before crossing the paint and never stop on it.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: For what single maneuver may a motorist cross a bike lane, and what check comes first?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Drivers may cross a bike lane only to turn, first checking alongside and behind with care.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What four safety benefits do sharrows promote, and how do they differ from dedicated bike lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Sharrows warn drivers that bikes share the lane, promote safe passing, and curb wrong-way riding and door crashes, yet unlike bike lanes they reserve no exclusive space.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: What is the core legal space difference between a striped bike lane and a painted sharrow?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Bike lanes grant cyclists exclusive marked space, while sharrows merely announce sharing with no exclusive zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Where does a green bike box sit, how wide is it, and how does it help cyclists?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Bike boxes are solid-green full-lane-width zones with a cyclist image beside the crosswalk at signalized intersections, giving riders a safe turning pocket.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What does a small bicycle detector symbol painted at a stop bar help a rider do?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: A pavement detector mark shows cyclists the sweet spot for tripping the traffic signal.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: How does green conflict paint along a bike lane differ in purpose from a green intersection bike box?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Green lane paint warns drivers crossing it, while the green bike box gives cyclists a full-width turning pocket at signals.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: How do bike-lane turn rules for drivers pair up with pavement detector marks for cyclists?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: Motorists may enter bike lanes only to turn with careful checks, while cyclists use detector marks to place themselves for a signal trigger.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Who bears legal responsibility for making sure a parked vehicle never becomes a traffic hazard?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: You own the duty to leave your parked car where it cannot turn into a road hazard.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Where should you look to park first, and how close to the curb must you sit when parking on a street?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Choose a marked parking area when one exists; forced onto the roadway, sit as far from traffic as you can, hugging within eighteen inches of any curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: How much clearance from live travel lanes does a safely parked car need?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Settle far enough from every travel lane that passing traffic flows past untouched.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: What check comes before opening a street-side door, and what safer exit option exists on busy streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Scan traffic before swinging a door open, and climb out on the curb side whenever needed.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How does Iowa rank marked parking stalls against roadside curb parking?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: A marked stall is the first parking choice, while roadway parking demands hugging within eighteen inches of the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Which two roadside cues mark restricted or time-limited parking zones?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Heed every posted parking ban or limit plus colored curb paint, since many no-park areas are signed that way.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Which two pedestrian and property access points are strictly off-limits for parking?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Never park on a crosswalk or square in front of any public or private driveway.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: Which bridges and underground roadways ban parking in Iowa?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Bridges beyond city limits and highway tunnels are both off-limits for parking.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Group Iowa's crosswalk-and-driveway bans against its rural-bridge-and-tunnel bans?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Crosswalks and driveway fronts ban parking for access, while out-of-town bridges and tunnels ban it for clearance.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: May you stop or park in the travel lane right beside a car already parked at the curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Pulling alongside another stopped or parked car to double-park is forbidden.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does legal curbside parking contrast with double parking?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Double parking beside another car is banned, while single-file parking belongs tight to the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What paint color commonly highlights signed no-parking zones, and can you ever park inside an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Stay out of signed no-parking zones, often flagged by yellow curbs or pavement lines, and never park inside an intersection.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: Which three walkways and high-speed roadways outlaw parking altogether?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Sidewalks, interstates, and highways all ban parking outright.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Why don't sidewalks or interstates need 'No Parking' signs posted every block to ban parking?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: Posted zones and intersections ban parking by sign, while sidewalks and interstates ban it by kind.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What credential is mandatory before pulling into a disability-reserved parking stall?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: A disability-reserved space is legal only with a Persons with Disabilities Parking Permit.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: Among all restricted parking spaces, which single one opens up with a special state permit?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: Only a disability permit opens a reserved space, while every other listed place stays closed to all.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: What minimum distance must you leave beside a fire hydrant in Iowa, plus any painted curb zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Keep at least five feet from a fire hydrant and stay out of any marked hydrant red zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: How many feet back from a stop sign must a parked car stay in Iowa?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Hold at least ten feet back from a stop sign.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: How far from a fire station entrance must you keep a parked vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Hold at least twenty feet back from a fire station entrance.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What minimum parking distance applies near a railroad crossing in Iowa?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Hold at least fifty feet back from a railroad crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Compare Iowa's shorter two parking clearance numbers for fire hydrants and stop signs?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: The hydrant needs five feet of clearance, while the stop sign needs ten feet.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: Compare Iowa's larger two parking clearance numbers for fire stations and railroad crossings?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: A firehouse mouth needs twenty feet of clearance, while a railroad crossing needs fifty feet.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: Which stopped vehicles with flashing lights trigger Iowa's move-over law?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Iowa move-over law orders a lane change past any stopped rig flashing its lights, from emergency, tow, recovery, maintenance, construction, and waste or recycling trucks down to an ordinary car blinking its hazards.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: What does Iowa's move-over law require when traffic or road layout makes changing lanes unsafe or impossible?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Where shifting lanes is impossible, illegal, or unsafe, slow to a reasonable and proper pace for conditions and stand ready to halt.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: Up to how long can Iowa suspend your license for violating the move-over law?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Breaking the move-over law can suspend your license for up to one year.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: How do the two compliance options rank under Iowa's move-over law?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Flashing stopped rigs demand a lane change first, while an impossible shift drops you to a slow, stop-ready crawl.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Why is assuming move-over applies only to red-and-blue police lights a mistake on the Iowa exam?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Tow and work rigs with flashers trigger move-over, and so does an ordinary car blinking its hazards.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: When unable to change lanes past a flashing vehicle, what speed standard applies and what license loss threatens violators?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: When a lane change cannot be made, is illegal or would be unsafe, slow to a speed that is reasonable for existing conditions and prepare to stop. A violation may lead to a license suspension lasting as long as one year.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: After a fender-bender with zero injuries, what must you do if your vehicle still drives safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: After a crash with nobody hurt, Iowa law makes you steer an operable car that can move safely out of the travel lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: By roughly what percentage does secondary-crash risk rise for each minute an interstate lane stays blocked?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Every minute a blocked interstate lane lingers, the chance of a second crash climbs by roughly two point eight percent.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: How does interstate secondary-crash math explain Iowa's 'Steer It, Clear It' rule for non-injury wrecks?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: Operable cars must clear the lanes after a no-injury crash, because each blocked minute lifts secondary-crash odds by roughly two point eight percent.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Where do blind spots lurk, and what vehicle parts and roadside features enlarge them?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Blind spots hide beyond mirror reach and grow from gear like posts and mirrors plus scenery like trees, sun, hedges, hills, and walls.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: How do you keep your car out of another driver's blind spot while cruising or passing?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.memory_hook: Pull ahead, drop back, pass briskly
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Refuse to cruise in another driver's blind spot by speeding up or dropping back, and hurry through it when passing.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Why must you never pace alongside a large truck or bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Never pace a truck or bus, whose giant blind zones can swallow your car unseen.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What habit should accompany every lane change and cross-traffic pullout in your own car?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Learn your own car's natural blind zones and treat every lane change and cross-traffic pullout as a blind-spot check.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Which daylight or weather factor swells blind spots worst, and what two tools counter it?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Weather and daylight swell blind spots, with windshield sun glare the worst offender, so deploy sunglasses or visors against it.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: What creates blind spots around your car, and what clears you from others' blind spots?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Gear and scenery build blind spots mirrors miss, while speed changes escape the blind spots of others.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How does passing a tractor-trailer safely contrast with pacing beside it?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Passing hurries through blind zones, while pacing big rigs camps inside them.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How do you counter your car's structural blind zones versus blinding windshield glare?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Known car zones demand checks at every maneuver, while sun glare demands shades and visors.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Why must every occupant buckle up before the car rolls an inch?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Buckle every soul before rolling, since crashes top teen killers and belting up is the cheapest escape from that count.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Where should a cinched lap belt rest normally and during pregnancy?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Cinched lap belts ride snug on hips, and expectant mothers wear them low across the pelvis beneath the belly.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Is riding unbuckled a primary offense in Iowa, and what fines apply for adults versus minors?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Beltless driving is a primary stoppable offense fining up to fifty dollars per rider and one hundred dollars per rider under eighteen.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Which front-seat and backseat passengers must wear seat belts under Iowa law?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Belts rank as the top lifesaver in crashes, and Iowa law demands them for every front-seat rider plus every backseat rider under eighteen.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: When does everyone buckle up, and where does the lap strap sit during pregnancy?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Everyone buckles before rolling, while lap belts ride hips and low pelvis in pregnancy.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: How do primary-stop per-rider fines enforce Iowa's front-seat and under-eighteen belt mandate?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Beltless riding draws a primary stop with per-rider fines, while belted riding obeys the front-seat and under-eighteen law.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Why is hoping to be thrown clear of a crash a dangerous myth?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Survivors stay inside: belts stop ejection into the path of other cars, beating the thrown-clear fantasy.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: How does one unbuckled rider or driver endanger everyone else in the car?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Belt choice affects all: loose riders turn projectile, and a lone loose driver can be flung from the seat into a crash.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Within what distance of home and speed zone do over half of traffic deaths happen?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Town trips kill too: over half of traffic deaths strike within twenty-five miles of home, many on roads under forty-five miles per hour

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: How do seat belts improve your odds of escaping a rare fire or water crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Belts free in under a second, and by keeping you conscious through fire or water crashes they improve escape odds.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: What two crash realities debunk skipping seat belts for yourself or backseat friends?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Staying belted inside beats ejection, while loose riders menace the whole cabin.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Why do short neighborhood errands and rare submerged-car fears both argue FOR wearing belts?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.memory_hook: Local roads kill, belts keep awake
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Near-home roads kill most, while quick-release belts aid escape by keeping you awake.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What age and weight combination requires a baby to ride strictly rear-facing in Iowa?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Babies under one year and under twenty pounds ride only in rear-facing restraints.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: How must children under age six be secured, and is a plain seat belt legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Children under six ride only in child restraints, meaning safety or booster seats and never a bare belt.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Where and how must youths ages six through seventeen be secured in a vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Children six through seventeen ride restrained or belted in every seat, front and back.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Who is barred from riding in the open cargo bed of a moving pickup truck?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: No one under eighteen may ride in the open bed of a moving pickup.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Which seating positions legally require adults eighteen and older to buckle up in Iowa?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Adults eighteen and up must belt in front seats.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: How does Iowa's infant rear-facing rule step up into the under-six child rule?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: Tiny babies face rearward under one year and twenty pounds, while under-six children sit in safety or booster seats.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: What two Iowa rules protect minors ages six through seventeen inside cabins and pickup beds?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: School-age minors belt or seat everywhere, while no minor rides a pickup bed.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: With how much force can an unsecured twenty-pound item slam forward in a sixty-mile-per-hour crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Strap down cabin cargo: at sixty miles per hour a twenty-pound object can slam with over one thousand pounds of force.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Why must you keep bottles and loose clutter off the driver-side floorboard?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Sweep floors clear so nothing rolls beneath the brake pedal and steals your brakes.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What are the three categories of driver distraction, with an everyday example of each?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Distraction splits three ways: visual eyes-off like GPS glances, manual hands-off like eating or makeup, and cognitive mind-off like music or chat.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Why are common behind-the-wheel distractions even riskier than one category alone?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Every distraction type endangers, and everyday wheel tasks often stack two or three at once.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Which three faculties do distractions steal, and how do cabin habits combine them?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Eyes, hands, and mind name the three distraction thieves, while real tasks often commit two at once.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: When is an Iowa driver legally allowed to read, type, or send texts, emails, or social posts?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Iowa bans writing, sending, or viewing electronic messages while driving; texts, emails, and posts wait until you halt fully off the traveled road.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Which three emergency or alert situations stay exempt from Iowa's electronic-message ban?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: The message ban spares on-duty public safety crews, emergency healthcare acts, and incoming safety, traffic, and weather alerts.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: Where must ordinary motorists stop for messages, and which three groups or alerts are spared?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: Messages wait for a full off-road stop, while safety crews, emergency medics, and alert receivers stay exempt.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What phone rule binds drivers under eighteen holding permits, intermediate, or minor school licenses?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen holding permits, intermediate, or special minor licenses may not call or talk while driving short of a full off-road stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: How is distracted driving enforced in Iowa, and what happens to your license or permit?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Distracted driving is a primary pull-over offense risking fines plus license or permit suspension or loss.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: How does Iowa's under-eighteen call ban pair with primary-offense enforcement for everyone?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: Young license holders face a total call ban short of stopping, while all drivers face primary-offense pullovers.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: What fine, license action, and felony exposure follow causing a death while driving distracted?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Distracted killing brings fines past one thousand dollars, license suspension, and possible vehicular homicide charges.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: Which six phone actions stay illegal under Iowa's hands-free rule, including voice video calls?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Hands-free law bans holding the phone, manual scrolling or typing, GPS address entry, video streaming or calls even by voice, viewing texts, videos, or social feeds, and any calling or dialing outside hands-free or voice control.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: Which five portable electronic device types fall under Iowa's distraction law?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: Covered electronic devices span cell phones, PDAs, tablets, gaming devices, and laptops.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: How do distracted-fatality penalties pair with Iowa's six banned phone interactions?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: Distracted killing tops one thousand dollars in fines with suspension and homicide exposure, while hands-free bans six phone interactions.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: How must adult calls and dialing operate in Iowa, why does video stay banned, and what devices count?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Iowa's hands-free rule forbids holding a phone or manually operating it while driving. Calls, texts and dialing require hands-free use or voice activation; video streaming and video calls remain prohibited even when voice-operated. Electronic devices include phones, personal digital assistants, tablets, gaming devices and laptops.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: Why is studying a handbook alone not enough to lower your crash risk?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: No book alone builds a safe driver; crash risk shrinks with experience earned through lessons and practice.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Why should you consult your vehicle's owner manual for proper starting steps?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Start the car by its owner manual, since steps differ with fuel injection and transmission type.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: What does each of Park, Reverse, Neutral, and Drive do on an automatic selector?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Automatics shift themselves while you pick Park to lock, Reverse to back, Neutral to idle, and Drive to go.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: What does Low gear do on an automatic transmission, and how might numbers label it?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Low caps engine speed and may appear as gears three, two, and one marking the top gear allowed.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: What builds safe driving habits over time, and what guides starting an unfamiliar car?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Experience, not reading, makes safe drivers, while starting steps vary by car and manual.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How do Park, Reverse, Neutral, and Drive differ in job from numbered Low positions?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Park, Reverse, Neutral, and Drive pick directions, while Low caps gears and may read three, two, one.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: How does a manual transmission step through speed ranges from Neutral upward?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Manual gears gate speed ranges, climbing Neutral and one through two, three, four, and beyond via the clutch third pedal.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: What three coordinated foot-and-hand steps complete a smooth manual gear shift?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Shift manuals in three beats: clutch down with the left foot, lever moved with the right hand, then gas eased as the clutch releases.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Besides upshifting, which three other maneuvers use the same manual clutch sequence?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Repeat the clutch dance to downshift, to halt, and to back up from Neutral or one into Reverse.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: How does the three-beat clutch routine handle both climbing speed and slowing or backing?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Manuals climb gears through the clutch, while the three-beat clutch dance also downshifts and reverses.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Why must you accelerate gradually instead of flooring jackrabbit starts?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Feed speed smoothly, since jackrabbit starts spin wheels and skid, especially on slick roads, and manuals demand clutch-gas balance against racing or stalling.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: What happens to tire traction under gradual throttle versus a jackrabbit launch?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Gentle throttle grips, while jackrabbit starts spin and skid.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: Which vehicle traits and human factor combine to determine how quickly you stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Stopping hinges on car weight, size, load, and tires plus your foot-to-brake reaction, and smooth halts take practice.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Which road surfaces can skid under harsh braking, and what does extra speed do?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Gravel, snow, ice, and even dry asphalt skid under harsh braking, and speed stretches every stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: What are Iowa's total reaction-plus-braking distances at twenty, thirty, and forty miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Stopping distance sums reaction and braking spans: sixty-nine feet at twenty miles per hour, one hundred twenty-three feet at thirty miles per hour, and one hundred eighty-nine feet at forty miles per hour

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What total stopping distances pile up at fifty, sixty, and seventy miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Higher speeds compound the sum: two hundred sixty-eight feet at fifty miles per hour, three hundred fifty-nine feet at sixty miles per hour, and four hundred sixty-four feet at seventy miles per hour

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How do vehicle mass and driver reflexes combine inside Iowa's speed-stopping chart?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Car bulk and reflexes set stops, while reaction plus braking sums tabled feet per speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: How should you use the brake pedal during an emergency stop with antilock brakes?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: With ABS, stomp and hold the pedal through its pushback without releasing, after studying the owner manual.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: How do you warn trailing drivers or tailgaters before a sudden slowdown ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Warn of surprise slows or tailgaters with three or four quick brake taps.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What general following cushion guards the space ahead, and under what conditions does it hold?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Hold a three- to four-second gap ahead where collisions lurk most, a rule valid only in normal traffic and fair weather.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: How does Iowa's minimum normal following time compare between beginning drivers and experienced drivers?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Beginners keep at least three seconds normally, while veterans may trim to two seconds in kind conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: At forty miles per hour, how many seconds does Iowa recommend normally versus on slick roads or behind big rigs?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: At forty miles per hour, the guide recommends leaving four to five seconds behind another vehicle. Increase this gap to at least six seconds for slippery conditions or when that vehicle obstructs your view.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: What weather limit bounds the three-to-four-second rule, and how do rookies differ from veterans?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Three-to-four-second gaps suit fair weather only, while beginners hold three and veterans may hold two.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How do forty-mile-per-hour cushions in rain pair with emergency antilock pedal technique?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: At forty miles per hour, the guide recommends leaving four to five seconds behind another vehicle; use at least six seconds for slippery conditions or an obstructed view. For a quick stop with antilock brakes, push the brake pedal as firmly as possible and continue holding it down.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: How do you use a fixed roadside object to verify a three-second following gap?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Time gaps by landmark: your bumper must not reach the marker before your slow count of three.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: At which three traffic signs or red signals must you always come to a complete stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Always halt at stop signs, flashing reds before proceeding if clear, and red lights even where right on red is legal.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: Where must you stop when leaving alleys or lots, and which two road workers command stops?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Also halt before sidewalks leaving private roads, entering public roads from drives and lots, for officers, and for work-zone flaggers.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: Which canes or service animal require an immediate full stop whenever a walker nears your path?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Halt for blind pedestrians with white or red-tipped canes or guide dogs whenever they near your path.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: How do quick brake-pedal taps contrast with your duty at stop signs and red signals?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Brake taps telegraph surprise slows, while signs and red lights always command halts.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Beyond signs and signals, which four driveway or human cues command a full stop?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: Drives, officers, and flaggers command halts, while blind pedestrians command them too.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: What weather do posted speed limits assume, and how does sixty compare with thirty in stopping room?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Posted limits cap legal speed for ideal roads, so temper pace to signs, surface, and sky; sixty miles per hour needs triple the stopping room of thirty miles per hour

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Why must you drop below posted signs in rain, and what stopping multiple hits at sixty?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Limits cap ideal-road speed, while sixty triples thirty's stopping room.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What are Iowa's unposted limits in business districts, residential or school zones, and suburbs or towing?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Unposted caps run twenty miles per hour in business zones, twenty-five miles per hour in residential and school zones, and forty-five miles per hour in suburbs and for towing rigs.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: What unposted Iowa limits govern fifty-, sixty-, and seventy-mile-per-hour roads by surface, time, and vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Further unposted caps run fifty miles per hour on dark unsurfaced secondaries and for trucks on secondaries anytime, sixty miles per hour on primaries, urban interstates, and daylit secondaries, and seventy miles per hour on rural interstates, with lower postings possible.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: Which zones step twenty, twenty-five, and forty-five in Iowa, and which vehicle shares forty-five?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Business, home, and suburb bands cap at twenty, twenty-five, and forty-five, while towing shares forty-five.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: How do fifty, sixty, and seventy unposted limits split across secondary, primary, and interstate highways?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: Without posted limits, the guide lists fifty miles per hour for unsurfaced secondary roads at night, from sunset until sunrise, and for all trucks using secondary roads regardless of time. It lists sixty miles per hour on all primary roads and urban interstate highways, plus secondary roads, including unpaved roads, from sunrise until sunset. Rural interstate highways have a seventy-mile-per-hour limit. Lower limits may be set for these conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: Why is crawling below traffic flow hazardous, and what minimum speed guards Iowa interstates?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Crawling crashes too, so match traffic flow, and shun interstates below their forty miles per hour minimum.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Which two clock-face hand positions keep steering safe around steering-wheel airbags?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Grip opposite wheel sides at nine and three or lower at seven and five to tame airbags and keep command.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: How far ahead should you scan for steering, and which two hand techniques turn corners?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Scan far ahead to pre-plan steering, and corner with hand-over-hand or push-pull.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Which two lazy steering habits surrender control during or after a turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Shun one-palm turns that surrender control, and unwind the wheel by hand rather than letting it slither free.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: What minimum speed protects interstates, and which two hand positions protect wrists?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: Crawlers match flow and shun interstates under forty, while grippers hold nine-and-three or seven-and-five.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: How do far scans and two-hand turns contrast with palm-spinning and letting the wheel slide?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: Far scans pre-plan steering with hand techniques, while palm spins and finger slips court loss.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Why must you back up slowly with light or zero throttle?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Reverse dulls control, so back slowly with a feathered or untouched pedal.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: Why must you look back past the headrest instead of relying only on mirrors and backup cameras?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Crane your head past the headrest, since mirrors and cameras alone crop the view and warp depth.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: How should you position your hips, arms, hands, and eyes when backing straight?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Twist hips around, drape the right arm over the seat, grip the wheel top left-handed, and sight over the right shoulder.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Where do you scan before and while backing, and how do your feet control movement?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Sweep behind and through blind zones before and during, then creep off the brake with gas only as needed.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Which direction do you turn the steering wheel when backing, and which glass tracks your path?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Aim the wheel where you want the tail to go while watching travel through the rear side glass.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: What two habits pair slow pedal control with direct vision during backing?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: Backing crawls on a feathered pedal, while head turns beat mirrors and cameras.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How do upper-body backing posture and brake-release creeping team up?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: The backing posture drapes an arm and sights over a shoulder, while checks and creep govern motion.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What three steps set up a clean intersection turn instead of a sudden dive?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Pre-pick your turn exit, bleed speed early, and scan for walkers and cars, shunning last-second sharp turns.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: What two path errors must you avoid while steering through a corner?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.memory_hook: Never cut short or swing wide
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Hold your arc: corner cutting and wide swings both invite crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: How do early turn preparation and steady lane arcs work together to prevent intersection crashes?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Planned turns pre-pick exits and bleed speed, while cut corners and wide swings invite crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Which four maneuvers require a turn signal, and why signal even when nobody looks nearby?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.memory_hook: Signal every move, blind spots hide
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Signal every lane change, turn, merge, and park to buy others reaction time, signaling even empty roads since blind zones may hide an audience.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: How many feet before a turn must you signal in Iowa at forty-five miles per hour or below versus higher speeds?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.memory_hook: Hundred feet slow, three hundred fast
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Iowa demands signals one hundred feet before turns where limits run forty-five miles per hour or less, and three hundred feet where limits run faster.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: How do you time your blinker around braking, earlier side drives, and completing the turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Blink before braking, yet past intervening streets, drives, and waiting entrants first, then kill the signal after turning.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: How does Iowa's universal signal habit pair with its speed-based footage thresholds?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.memory_hook: Always blink, hundred or three hundred
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Every direction change earns a signal even on empty roads, while slow zones need one hundred feet and fast zones three hundred.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: What comes before braking, after side driveways, and right after straightening out?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Signals precede braking yet follow side streets and waiting cars, while dead signals get cancelled.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: Under what three conditions may you turn right at a red light in Iowa?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Red lights allow right turns after a full stop and full yield unless a no-turn-on-red sign forbids.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What exact street-and-lane setup allows a left turn on red in Iowa?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Red lights allow left turns only from a one-way left lane onto another one-way street.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: How does Iowa's rule for turning left on red add extra restrictions beyond turning right on red?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Rights on red need stops and yields short of bans, while lefts on red need one-way to one-way geometry.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: What two conditions must both hold before making a U-turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: U-turn only where unprohibited and safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: Why does the Iowa manual advise driving to the next intersection instead of making a three-point turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Three-point turns court collisions, so favor the next intersection instead.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: How does the manual treat open U-turns compared with mid-block three-point turns?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: U-turns pass where legal and safe, while three-pointers lose to the next intersection.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: Which maneuvers count as lane moves, and how many lanes may you shift across at once?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Lane moves span lane swaps, ramp merges, and curb entries; shift one lane at a time into confirmed gaps while yielding to occupants.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: How should you manage your signal, speed, and eyes throughout a lane change?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Announce with signals and hold pace unless dropping to a slower lane, scanning throughout for surprises.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: What two threats are you looking for in your rearview and side mirrors before changing lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Clear rearview and side mirrors of target-lane cars and imminent passers.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: How do you check your blind spot without drifting out of your current lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Shoulder-check the move side for rear-corner lurkers while pinning the wheel straight against arm-follow reflex.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: On a road with three or more lanes, why must you also check the far lane beyond your target lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Also scan the far lane for rivals diving at your same gap.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: What pairs single-lane movement with predictable speed during merges and lane swaps?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.memory_hook: One confirmed gap, steady signaled pace
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Lane moves shift singly into yielded gaps, while signals and steady pace announce them.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: How do mirror checks and straight-wheel shoulder checks cover different zones before moving over?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.memory_hook: Mirrors spot behind, shoulders clear corners
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Mirrors clear lanes and passers, while shoulder checks pin rear corners with a straight wheel.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: Before moving into a center lane on a multi-lane highway, what extra lane check prevents a simultaneous merge crash?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: Before a lane change, check an additional lane farther over, if one exists: a driver there could be trying to enter the same lane you intend to use.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: What three questions must all be yes before you start to pass another vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.memory_hook: Legal markings, clear room, real need
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: Pass only where signs and markings bless it, room truly allows, and need demands.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: How many vehicles should you overtake per pass, and what roadside openings should make you hold back?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: Take one car per pass and shun zones where cross traffic may pop from intersections and drives.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: What four steps launch a safe pass from behind a slower vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: Open a pass by confirming open lane ahead, clearing mirrors and blind zones, then signaling and accelerating in.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: When is it safe to steer back into the right lane after passing, and what do you do once back?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Mid-pass watch fore, aft, and mirror, then re-enter gently once the passed nose shows in your mirror, cancel, and settle to safe speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: What combines the three pre-pass checks with single-vehicle passing limits?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Passes need permission, room, and need, while single victims and entry-free zones bound them.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: How do the checks for pulling out to pass pair with the cue for returning right?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: Pass entries confirm space, mirrors, signals, and speed, while exits await mirror-visible noses and gentle returns.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: Which white and yellow lane markings permit passing from your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.memory_hook: Broken white or dashed yellow side
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: Broken white lines in your lane bless same-direction passes, while solid-and-broken yellow pairs bless only the dashed side.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: What does a double solid yellow center line forbid, and how do yellow and white lines split traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Double yellow centers ban both directions, with yellow dividing foes and white dividing friends.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: Compare passing rules across broken white, mixed solid-broken yellow, and double solid yellow lines?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.memory_hook: White passes, dashed passes, double blocks
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: Broken white blesses same-way passes and dashed yellow blesses its side, while double yellow bans all.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: What two terrain features forbid passing because they hide oncoming traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Never pass cresting hills or rounding blind curves.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: Within one hundred feet of which five roadway structures or crossings is passing illegal in Iowa?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: Never pass within one hundred feet of signed narrow bridges, viaducts, tunnels, railroad crossings, or intersections.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What side is off-limits for passing, and how should you treat questionable oncoming gaps?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: Never pass on the right nor into oncoming gaps too tight to survive.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: Group Iowa's terrain bans, hundred-foot structure bans, and side-or-gap passing bans together?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: Hills and curves blind passes, while hundred-foot zones, right sides, and tight gaps ban them.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: What percentage of serious crashes stem from human choices or mistakes, making defensive driving essential?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Defensive driving keeps you aware and ready, since ninety-four percent of serious crashes trace to human choices and errors.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: What actions define the first defensive driving habit of thinking safety first?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: First, think safety: shun aggression and inattention, bank space ahead, and belt against ejection.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: How far ahead in seconds should you read traffic, and how should your eyes work to stay aware?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Second, stay aware: sweep mirrors often, read twenty to thirty seconds ahead, and keep eyes roaming.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: How should you respond to an aggressive driver, and which vulnerable users must stay on your radar?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.memory_hook: Give space, pull off, watch walkers
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Dodge aggressive drivers by slowing, pulling over, or exiting safely, while tracking walkers, riders, and animals.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: What does the third defensive habit say about trusting other drivers at red lights and stop signs?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Third, trust no one: expect red-light and stop-sign runners and plan every move for the worst case.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: How many seconds of following distance does Iowa's fourth defensive habit recommend?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Fourth, hold the three- to four-second gap for reaction room.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: Why must you cut speed below posted limits when road or weather conditions deteriorate?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Fifth, temper speed to conditions below ideal-road limits, since pace erodes control when trouble strikes.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: What does banking an escape route mean for positioning your vehicle in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Sixth, bank an escape route: sit seen and seeing with an alternate path for sudden blocks.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: What does the seventh defensive driving habit require regarding distractions?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Seventh, kill distractions and grant driving your whole mind.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: How does the ninety-four-percent human-error crash statistic connect to safety-first habits?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Human error drives ninety-four percent of bad crashes, while safety-first habits blunt it.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: How do twenty-to-thirty-second visual scans pair with stepping aside from aggressive drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Mirrors and long scans feed awareness, while aggressive drivers get dodged by slowing or exiting.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How do expecting stop-sign runners and holding a three-to-four-second gap reinforce each other?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Distrust plans for signal runners, while three-to-four-second gaps buy reaction time.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: Which three habits finish the defensive list, and why is obeying speed signs alone not enough?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Low speed, escape routes, and full focus close the seven, while limits alone never suffice.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Why is driving at a uniform lawful pace with surrounding traffic safer than going much faster or slower?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Match traffic pace, since speed outliers breed lane swaps, passes, tailgating, and crashes; uniform lawful speed is safest.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: How should you adjust when you spot slower traffic ahead instead of waiting until the last moment?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Adapt pace early to slow traffic with lane moves or gentle braking, never sudden stomps.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Which five types of slow-moving vehicles appear on Iowa roads, and what warning emblems or lights mark them?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Farm rigs, horse carts, ATVs, UTVs, and road crews creep, often flying orange triangles or flashers.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: Why is tailgating dangerous, and how should your following count change as speeds climb?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Tailgating kills stopping room, so judge gaps by the three-four-second rule with longer spans at speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: What four calm steps help shake a tailgater riding closely behind you?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.memory_hook: Edge right, signal early, let pass
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: When tailgated, edge right for their view, telegraph moves early, slow to invite a pass, or leave the flow.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: What happens to crash risk when everyone holds a uniform lawful speed versus driving as an outlier?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Uniform lawful pace calms roads, while outliers multiply conflicts.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Why must you spot orange slow-moving triangles or rear flashers from far back on rural highways?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.memory_hook: Spot triangles early, avoid hard stops
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Farm vehicles, horse-drawn vehicles, ATVs, UTVs and road-maintenance vehicles typically move slowly and may display an orange triangle or flashing rear lights. Notice them early so you can slow or change lanes safely; abrupt slowing can cause a collision.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: How do you prevent tailgating ahead while managing someone tailgating behind?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.memory_hook: Hold four ahead, invite pass behind
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Gaps stop tailgating crashes, while the tailgated edge right and telegraph moves.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: What two things must every driver communicate to surrounding traffic, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Broadcast presence and plans, since unseen and surprising moves cause crashes.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Why must you turn headlights on manually during daytime fog, rain, or bright snow glare?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Headlights show you the dark and show you to others, so burn them through fog, rain, and snow, overriding auto lamps in bright snow glare.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: At what times, visibility footage, and wiper use does Iowa law require both headlights on?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Iowa law lights both beams sunset to sunrise and whenever sight drops to five hundred feet or less; wipers on means lights on.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Which four situations involving drifting walkers, passers, distracted drivers, or blind alleys call for your horn?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Sound the horn for lane-drifting walkers and riders, passers swerving at you, inattentive or half-blind drivers, and blind alley mouths.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: What three additional danger situations, including losing control of your own car, call for sounding the horn?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.memory_hook: Sound horn for threats or skids
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Also horn cars threatening you, anyone needing your presence announced, and your own runaway slides toward people.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: If your vehicle breaks down, how do you position and light it, and which terrain spots must you avoid?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Broken down, flee the roadway if able, blaze hazards, and park only where approaching eyes can see, never past crests or bends.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: If your vehicle stalls dead inside a moving travel lane and cannot roll off, what must everyone do?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Stalled in a lane, march everyone out fast to ground far from shoulders and traffic, then call the authorities.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: How does broadcasting presence and plans tie directly to daytime weather headlight use?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: Presence and plans get broadcast, while headlights serve seeing and being seen.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Combine Iowa's mandatory headlight triggers with the purpose of its seven horn-warning scenarios?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.memory_hook: Five hundred sight, horn prevents strikes
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Night and five hundred-foot murk mandate beams, while horns warn seven listed hazards.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: How does handling a breakdown that reaches the roadside differ from a car stuck inside a travel lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Breakdowns flee roadsides with blazing hazards, while lane strandings march out and call.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: How should you pass oncoming vehicles on a narrow unmarked rural gravel road?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Meet gravel oncoming on narrow unmarked lanes by slowing, hugging right as safe, and braving dust clouds.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: Why must you approach rural bridges ready to stop before crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Treat rural bridges as one-car squeezes narrower than the road, stopping for oncoming users.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: Compare meeting oncoming traffic on open narrow gravel against meeting traffic at a narrow rural bridge?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.memory_hook: Gravel hugs right, narrow bridge waits
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: On narrow gravel roads in rural areas, reduce speed and keep as far right as safety allows when meeting traffic. Approach narrow bridges cautiously and be ready to stop for an oncoming vehicle because some bridges can carry only one vehicle at once.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: How do off-highway rural hills and curves differ from main highways, and what should you do beforehand?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Pre-slow and right-hug before hill crests and curves, which run steeper and sharper off-highway.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: Why must you slow, look both ways, and be ready to stop at rural railroad crossings?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.memory_hook: No gates or bells, look twice
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: Cross rural tracks only after slowing, double-looking, and readying to stop, since lights, bells, gates, and markings usually miss.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: Pair your approach to steep rural crests and curves with your approach to bare country railroad crossings?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.memory_hook: Slow right at crests, scan tracks
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: Hills and curves pre-slow rightward, while bare rural crossings double-look and ready stops.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: Why does overtaking wide farm machinery require extreme caution even on an open rural stretch?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.memory_hook: Watch wide implements and left turns
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: Farm rigs, ATVs, bikes, horse carts, and work crews creep rural roads, so spot them early, slow down, and pass farm giants with extreme care past their wide unmarked turns, road-wide bodies, and faint signals.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: What speed, gap, mirror, headlight, and eye habits keep driving safe after dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.memory_hook: Slow, widen gaps, track right stripe
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Dark driving slows pace, stretches gaps, fights glare by right-looking and mirror tilts, lights up before sunset, saves high beams for lonely roads, and answers blinding with slower speed and right-edge stripes.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: Contrast what protects you around slow rural machinery with what protects you against night glare?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.memory_hook: Spot tractors early, track edge stripe
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: Creeping farm and work traffic gets early spotting, while night wants low beams, long gaps, and stripe tracking.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: When are animals most active, and why should you hold your lane instead of swerving if you cannot stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.memory_hook: Dawn-dusk peak, brake straight, never swerve
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: Watch animals hardest at dawn and dusk; given no stop room, hold course since swerves worsen crashes, and after strikes run crash protocol.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: Which animal leads Iowa wildlife crashes, which three months peak, and why keep scanning after seeing one?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: Deer top Iowa wildlife crashes, peaking in October, November, and May yet striking year-round in groups that demand extra scanning.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: Connect Iowa's peak deer months and dawn-dusk hours with the no-swerve survival rule?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Surprise animals hold course unswerved, while deer peaks span fall months plus May.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: Who suffers seventy-eight percent of deaths in large-truck crashes, and how do you check semi blind spots?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: Car riders absorb seventy-eight percent of truck-crash deaths, so grant big rigs wide respect and shun their front, back, and side no-zones, remembering mirror invisibility cuts both ways.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: Why do big trucks need far longer braking room, and when may you merge back in front of one?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.memory_hook: Wait for full cab in mirror
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: Trucks out-brake you in distance, so re-enter only past a mirror-full truck nose and never cut their bows.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: Why do right-turning semi-trucks swing left first, and what gap must you never squeeze into?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.memory_hook: Never squeeze between truck and curb
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: Right-turning trucks first swing left, blind to tail and flank sitters, so never thread truck and curb and mind their signals.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: How does the seventy-eight-percent fatality stat explain staying clear of front, rear, and side no-zones?
