sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: Car riders take truck-crash deaths mostly, while no-zones ring rigs on three sides.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: Pair the rule for returning in front of a passed truck with the rule for right-turning trucks?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.memory_hook: Full nose mirror, clear right curb
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: Passes return past mirror-full noses, while right turns swing left past curb squeezers.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: Why are intersections high-risk for motorcycles, and why must you distrust a motorcycle's turn signal?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: Honor motorcycle space, treat intersections as prime collision ground by confirming sight and speed, and distrust sticky signals until intent shows.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: What following gap does a motorcycle need, why add more in rain, and how much lane width does passing take?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: Trail bikes by three to four seconds, farther when wet for two-wheel wobble, and pass only with full spare lanes unshared.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: Summarize intersection caution, following gap, and lane width when sharing roads with motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.memory_hook: Verify turns, four seconds, full lane
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: Bikes earn space, intersection care, and signal distrust, while trails gap three-plus seconds.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: Which foot and wheeled users must you scan for and yield to at intersections and driveways?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: Scan intersections and drives for walkers, riders, skaters, wheelchairs, and micro-devices, then yield them the right-of-way.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: Why must you never pass a vehicle stopped or slowing near a crosswalk?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: Never overtake cars stopped or slowing for pedestrians you cannot yet see.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: Combine active driveway-and-corner scanning with the ban on passing stopped crosswalk vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.memory_hook: Scan every crossing, never pass stops
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: Crossings scan for wheels and feet with yields, while stopped cars for walkers never get passed.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: Why are bicycles riding in street lanes, and how must you pass and return around one?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.memory_hook: Change lanes fully, mirror before return
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: Bikes belong on roads, often barred from sidewalks, so pass only via full lane changes and return right only past mirror-visible riders.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: When are bicyclists hardest to spot, and what maneuver demands an extra right-side blind-spot check?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.memory_hook: Watch night reflectors, check right turns
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: Hunt night reflectors and lights plus rear blind spots, hardest before right turns.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: Tie together how you overtake a cyclist ahead and how you protect one before turning right?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.memory_hook: Full lane pass, check right blind
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: Bicycles take full lanes on passes, while nights and right turns double-watch them.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: How hot can an enclosed cabin get within ten minutes or on a seventy-eight-degree day, and what rescue does Iowa allow?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.memory_hook: Over one-sixty fast, rescue glass legal
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: Never cage kids, elders, dependents, or pets in parked cars, whose cabins top one hundred sixty degrees within ten minutes and hit one hundred on mild seventy-eight-degree days; heatstroke kills, so call nine one one and know Iowa lets rescuers smash windows.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: Who must never be left alone in an enclosed vehicle, and what two actions save someone trapped?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.memory_hook: Never leave anyone, call, break glass
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: Never leave a child, an older person, a dependent person or a pet alone inside an enclosed vehicle. Depending on heat and humidity, the cabin can exceed one hundred sixty degrees in under ten minutes; even a seventy-eight-degree day can raise the interior to one hundred degrees in minutes. Iowa permits breaking a vehicle window to give medical attention to a trapped person or animal.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: How can you check real-time road and plow conditions across Iowa before starting a bad-weather trip?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.memory_hook: Check Iowa traveler app and cameras
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: Pre-study weather trips via Iowa traveler info online and in-app around the clock, scouting plow and traffic cameras firsthand.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: If you cannot postpone a storm drive, what five precautions protect you?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.memory_hook: Slow, widen gap, disable cruise, kit
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: Forced into storms, slow down, stretch gaps, kill cruise, maintain the car, and pack a winter emergency kit.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: Pair pre-trip weather scouting with your behind-the-wheel storm adjustments?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.memory_hook: Scout cameras first, kill cruise driving
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: Trips pre-study traveler info and cams, while forced storm runs slow, gap, kill cruise, and pack kits.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: What following gap, beam, cruise, defroster, and glance habits apply on wet pavement?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.memory_hook: Five-to-six seconds, low beams, no cruise
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: Wet roads want prompt wipers, low beams, slower pace, five-to-six-second gaps, gentle curves and crossings, defrosted glass, dead cruise, and only clear-road one-second glances.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: What causes tires to hydroplane, and what three visual road clues warn you to slow down?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.memory_hook: Water deeper than tread lifts tires
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: Water past tread depth planes tires into skids, so slow at deep puddles, shiny pavement, or vanished leader tracks.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: Connect Iowa's five-to-six-second wet following gap with what happens when water exceeds tread depth?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.memory_hook: Six-second rain gap, watch vanishing tracks
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: Wet wants wipers, low beams, five-plus gaps, and dead cruise, while planing water outslicks tread.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: How little moving water can sweep away even an SUV or pickup, and what if your car stalls in floodwater?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.memory_hook: Six inches sweeps trucks, climb high
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: Vehicles account for nearly half of flash-flood deaths. As little as six inches of moving water may carry a vehicle away, including a sport utility vehicle or pickup. Do not cross a flooded roadway or bridge; turn back and choose another route. Leave a vehicle that stalls in floodwater and head to higher ground.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: If floodwater sweeps your vehicle under water, what steps let you open the door and escape?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.memory_hook: Stay calm, equalize cabin, push out
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: Swept under, stay calm, let the cabin flood, push doors open, hold breath, and swim up.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: Which lights work in fog, which lights must stay off, and when should you leave the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.memory_hook: Low or fog beams, never highs
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: Fog wants low or fog beams never high ones, sight-matched speed, and parking off-road when needed.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: How does a tornado watch differ from a tornado warning, and what is a driver's best shelter?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.memory_hook: Watch means possible, warning means imminent
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: Tornado watches mean possible twisters and warnings mean imminent ones via broadcasts, radios, and sirens; drivers best shelter in sturdy buildings.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: If a tornado strikes on the open road with no building nearby, what are your two options and what structure is banned?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.memory_hook: Duck low or ditch, skip overpasses
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: Shelterless, pull over, duck belted below glass shielding heads, or ditch-crouch after safe exits, always shunning bridges and overpasses.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.front: Review the key trap in flash floods, dense fog, and tornado alerts?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.memory_hook: Six-inch floods, low beams, skip overpasses
sec16-card-sec16-R13.expected_back: Floods float trucks in inches and ban crossings, while fog bans high beams and tornadoes rank watches below warnings.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: What must you clear off your vehicle before driving in winter, and why do bridges freeze before roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.memory_hook: Clear all snow, bridges freeze first
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: Strip every flake off glass and lamps, and fear invisible black ice, which bridges and overpasses grow first from double-sided frost.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: How do you start moving and brake on snow or ice, and how much can icy stopping distance multiply?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.memory_hook: Straight gentle inputs, up to tenfold
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: Launch straight and gentle, slow for lost grip, kill cruise, brake early only rolling straight, and hang far back against tenfold stops and skids.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.front: Combine full snow clearing, bridge black ice, and straight-wheel ice inputs?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.memory_hook: Clean windows, watch bridges, steer straight
sec16-card-sec16-R14.expected_back: Snow strips cars bare and black ice ambushes bridges first, while launches stay straight and gentle.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: How fast do snowplows typically work, why never pass on the shoulder side, and what sticks out?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: Plows plod near twenty-five to thirty-five miles per hour inviting rear-enders, so approach gently, never pass shoulder-side, grant blind spotted snowy room, and pass wide of jutting blades.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: If snow strands your car on the highway, where should you wait and what location clues help dispatchers?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.memory_hook: Stay belted inside, call with mileposts
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: Snowbound, shoulder-park, stay belted inside as findable shelter, and phone nine one one with exits, mileposts, or landmarks.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.front: Pair safe spacing around slow snowplows with survival rules if a blizzard strands your car?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.memory_hook: Give plows room, stay belted inside
sec16-card-sec16-R15.expected_back: Plows plod near thirty miles per hour with wide berths, while stranding stays belted inside and phones out.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.front: Why must even careful defensive drivers know emergency maneuvers before trouble strikes?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.expected_back: Emergencies find even careful drivers, so readiness decides outcomes.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.front: What steering, throttle, and brake inputs bring a vehicle safely off the road after a blowout?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.memory_hook: Grip straight, ease gas, feather brake
sec17-card-sec17-F02.expected_back: Blow a tire and clamp the wheel straight, coast off the gas with feathered brakes, and flee the roadway to safety.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.front: Which way does a front-tire blowout pull your car, and what steering mistake must you resist?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.expected_back: Front blowouts yank toward the flat, so resist overcorrection, re-straighten, and ease onto the right shoulder fast.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.front: Combine general blowout pedal control with the steering rule for a blown front tire?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.expected_back: Flats hold straight and coast off-road, while front blows demand no overcorrection.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.front: What switches and backup lamps should you try while pulling off if your headlights fail?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.expected_back: Dead headlights get switch retries, high-beam trials, flashers or fog lamps, and a quick roadside exit.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.front: Do steering and brakes stop working completely if your engine stalls in motion?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.expected_back: Stalled engines keep heavy-but-working steering and brakes, so muscle off the road with hard pedal pressure.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.front: Contrast your immediate actions when headlights go dark versus when the engine stalls?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.memory_hook: Test backup lights, muscle heavy pedals
sec17-card-sec17-R02.expected_back: Dark lamps retry switches and beams before flashing and exiting, while stalls muscle heavy controls roadside.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.front: In what order do you handle a stuck accelerator so you do not lose power steering in traffic?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.memory_hook: Shift neutral, pull off, shut down
sec17-card-sec17-F06.expected_back: Runaway throttles want eyes forward, a snap to neutral, a safe pull-off, and engine shutdown after stopping.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.front: Why must neither you nor a passenger ever pull the ignition key out while the car is rolling?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.expected_back: Never yank keys or let riders grab them rolling, since locked wheels crash cars.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.front: Why is shifting to neutral the cure for a runaway throttle while yanking the key is disastrous?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.memory_hook: Neutral cuts power, key locks steering
sec17-card-sec17-R03.expected_back: Stuck throttles snap neutral before stopping and killing engines, while key yanks lock wheels entirely.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.front: If the brake pedal drops with no stopping power, what two actions do you try first?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.expected_back: Dead pedals get pumping first, then slow parking-brake drags released at any skid.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.front: If pumping and the parking brake still leave you rolling, how do you finish stopping and what comes after?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.memory_hook: Downshift off road, do not drive
sec17-card-sec17-F09.expected_back: Still rolling, downshift to a safe off-road halt and park brakeless cars for good.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.front: Name all three brake-failure steps in exact order from first pedal try to final stop?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.expected_back: Dead brakes pump, then drag parking brakes skid-ready, then downshift off-road for good.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.front: What single priority comes first immediately after any collision?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.expected_back: Crash triage starts with everybody's safety.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.front: If your car can still move safely after a minor crash, where should it go and what do you shut off?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.memory_hook: Move off lanes, shut engine down
sec17-card-sec17-F11.expected_back: First clear lanes if possible, shutting the car down and still.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.front: What three pieces of information should you report immediately when calling nine-one-one after a crash?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.expected_back: Then phone nine one one with injuries, location, and details.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.front: Put post-crash safety priority, clearing lanes, and calling nine-one-one in order?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.expected_back: Safety triages first with lanes cleared and cars stilled, while nine one one takes injuries and places.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.front: Which crashes require an Iowa accident report, what is the dollar threshold, and what is the filing deadline?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.expected_back: State law reports injury, death, or damage past one thousand five hundred dollars, and missing the seventy-two-hour window costs privileges plus penalties.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.front: Which three documents must you provide to investigating officers at a collision?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.expected_back: Hand officers insurance, registration, and license.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.front: Whom should you contact after handling officers and reports to cover liability obligations?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.expected_back: Finally brief your insurer on liability and at-fault obligations to others.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.front: Tie together Iowa's mandatory report triggers, the three officer documents, and calling your insurer?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.expected_back: Injury, death, or one thousand five hundred dollars damage compels reports within seventy-two hours, while officers take papers and insurers take briefs.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.front: What demeanor and response should you maintain during any interaction with law enforcement?

sec17-card-sec17-F17.front: How do optional autism or deaf-and-hard-of-hearing indicators on Iowa records help during a traffic stop?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.memory_hook: License and screen alerts aid communication
sec17-card-sec17-F17.expected_back: Autism and deaf indicators on licenses and police screens prime officers for smoother stops.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.front: How do calm driver behavior and optional communication indicators work together during a stop?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.expected_back: Officer meetings stay calm and obedient, while autism and deaf flags prime smoother stops.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.front: When patrol lights signal you to stop on a busy road, what kind of spot should you choose?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.memory_hook: Clear travel lanes, pick safe lot
sec17-card-sec17-F18.expected_back: Signaled stops pull clear of lanes when safe, favoring lots or side streets on busy roads.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.front: Once parked for a traffic stop, what should you do with the engine and your hands?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.memory_hook: Shut engine off, hands on wheel
sec17-card-sec17-F19.expected_back: Then kill the engine, show hands on the wheel, stay calm, and obey.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.front: Connect where you pull over for police lights with what you do the moment the car stops?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.memory_hook: Safe lot, engine off, visible hands
sec17-card-sec17-R08.expected_back: Signal stops pull clear of lanes into lots or side streets, while engines die and hands show.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.front: Summarize the full four-part procedure from seeing flashing police lights behind you to speaking with the officer?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.memory_hook: Pull clear, shut off, hands visible
sec17-card-sec17-R09.expected_back: When a law-enforcement vehicle signals you to stop, carefully move into a clear area when safe, away from the travel lane. Shut off the vehicle, keep your hands in sight, preferably on the steering wheel, and remain calm while following the officer's directions.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Which drivers must hold a permit or license before operating on public roads in Iowa?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Operating any motor vehicle, motorcycle, or moped on public pavement without valid credentials invites an immediate traffic citation.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: When may an armed-forces member drive in Iowa without holding an Iowa driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Test writers try extending military exemptions to off-duty errands, yet only official military rigs driven on duty qualify.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Under what distance and trip limit may farm machinery use Iowa roads without a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Exceeding the short two-mile radius between the home farm and nearby fields strips away the farm-equipment licensing exemption.
sec01-card-sec01-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Home farm trips within two miles

visual_sync.text_span: Home farm trips within two miles

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: What credential lets an out-of-state visitor or student legally drive on Iowa roadways?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Out-of-state students and tourists stay legal behind the wheel only while their home state or country credential remains valid.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How does Iowa's military exemption change when a service member switches from an on-duty rig to a personal car?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Driving your own sedan to dinner is never on-duty military transport, so standard licensing rules snap right back on.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: When does driving farm equipment on public roads in Iowa require a valid driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Hauling equipment down public highways outside the two-mile home-farm link demands a licensed operator behind the wheel.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: How does registering to vote in Iowa affect your residency status for driver licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Joining local voter rolls declares Iowa your home right away, ending any claim that you are merely passing through.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: What happens to your driver-licensing status when you enroll a child in an Iowa public school?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Putting your kid into an Iowa public classroom immediately classifies you as a state resident who needs local licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: How does accepting permanent employment in Iowa change your status for driver licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Starting a permanent local paycheck ends visitor status, meaning your out-of-state wallet card cannot cover long-term commuting.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: How many unbroken days of living in Iowa make you a resident for driver-licensing rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Applicants often guess sixty or ninety days, yet thirty straight days of living in Iowa triggers licensing residency.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Which two property tax exemption claims count you as an Iowa resident for driver licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Filing for a local homestead or military property tax break tells the state you live here permanently for licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: What does receiving state public assistance mean for your Iowa driver-licensing residency?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Accepting state-funded assistance anchors your legal residence in Iowa, triggering the requirement to hold an Iowa license.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: How many residency conditions must you meet before Iowa counts you as a resident for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Exam questions try stacking multiple ties together, when hitting even one listed condition makes you an Iowa resident.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does a newcomer's licensing status shift once they reach thirty continuous days in Iowa?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Before any trigger hits you may drive on a home license, yet day thirty flips you into resident rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Why can someone become an Iowa resident on day one without waiting thirty continuous days?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Voting, public-school enrollment, permanent work, tax exemptions, or state aid each establish residency immediately without waiting a month.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Do you have to claim both homestead and military property tax exemptions to trigger Iowa residency?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Both property tax breaks stand as independent triggers, so claiming just one on Iowa land establishes licensing residency.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: When are you required to carry your driver's license or learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Leaving your wallet at home for a two-minute grocery run still counts as driving without proof of licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Besides your license or permit, which two documents must stay with the vehicle in paper or digital form?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Iowa accepts digital or paper liability cards alongside current registration, sparing you a ticket during roadside stops.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: What two penalties can strike if you get pulled over without required license, registration, or insurance proof?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Driving without required credentials or coverage proof risks expensive court fines and watching a tow truck impound your ride.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: What distinct legal fact does each of your three required driving documents prove at a traffic stop?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Officers verify both the human and the machine, so driver authority, valid registration, and liability proof must travel together.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which physical screening must every applicant complete when applying for an Iowa driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Spotting lane lines and hazards safely starts with clear sight, so nobody skips the vision check at application.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which exam must every applicant pass before qualifying for an Iowa driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Road safety depends on shared traffic rules, meaning every licensing candidate must pass the written knowledge check first.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Which age group must prove completion of a state-approved driver education course to get licensed?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Applicants younger than eighteen cannot advance to full teen licensing without certified proof of state-approved driver education.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: When can an Iowa license applicant skip taking a separate behind-the-wheel driving evaluation?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Completing approved driver education already evaluates your road skills, waiving a separate behind-the-wheel drive at licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Which special licensing program governs Iowa drivers under age eighteen, with full rules posted online?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Teens build solo experience step by step under the Graduated Driver's License Program detailed on the state website.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Between the knowledge check and the behind-the-wheel drive, which one can driver education waive and which never drops?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Finishing driver education can satisfy your road-driving evaluation, yet no applicant ever gets a waiver from knowledge testing.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How does the manual distinguish completing the vision screening from taking the knowledge requirement?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Staff run a vision check when you apply, whereas the knowledge portion requires earning a passing score.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How do state-approved driver education and the Graduated Driver's License Program differ for under-eighteen drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Don't blur the two terms, because driver education is the training class while graduated licensing is the multi-stage framework.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What free study resource does the Iowa DOT post on its website to help applicants prepare?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Running drills on the DOT website reveals weak spots in road signs and rules before your licensing sitting.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: What does Iowa's Skip the Trip program allow eligible applicants to complete from home or school?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Skip the Trip saves a service-center visit by letting eligible students complete their knowledge requirement at home or school.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: How does Iowa treat moped credentials and commercial credentials compared with a standard license?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Moped riders and commercial truckers follow dedicated requirement lists posted separately on the Iowa DOT website.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: Where does the Iowa driver's manual direct motorists to find current timing and steps for license renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Renewal windows and online eligibility rules update over time, so the manual points straight to the DOT website.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: How does the DOT online study tool differ from Iowa's Skip the Trip option?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Confusing the warmup drill with Skip the Trip leaves you uncredited, since only Skip the Trip counts toward licensing.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: How are rectangular rapid-flashing beacons activated, and at what kinds of crossings are they installed?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Pedestrians trigger bright side-to-side strobes on busy multi-lane streets that lack full overhead traffic lights.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What two duties kick in the instant a crosswalk beacon's amber lights start strobing?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Scanning both curb ramps catches a second jogger or cyclist stepping off right behind the first walker.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: On a pedestrian hybrid beacon, what do dark lenses, a blinking bottom yellow, and a steady bottom yellow tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Recognizing the two-stage yellow sequence lets you brake smoothly instead of panic-stopping when twin reds light.
sec06-card-sec06-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Dark proceed, blink slow, steady prepare

visual_sync.text_span: Dark proceed, blink slow, steady prepare

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: How does your stop duty change when a hybrid beacon's twin top reds shift from steady to alternating blink?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Alternating wig-wag reds work just like a stop sign once pedestrians finish crossing, keeping traffic flowing safely.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How does a rectangular rapid-flashing beacon's light pattern differ from a pedestrian hybrid beacon?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Knowing both systems prevents hesitation at HAWK overhead clusters that stay dark until triggered.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Why doesn't an unlit pedestrian hybrid beacon act like a broken four-way stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Unlike a power-outage traffic light, a sleeping hybrid beacon stays dark by design until someone presses the button.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How does proceeding past strobing amber beacons compare with proceeding under blinking twin red hybrid lamps?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Blinking twin reds always require one complete stop before rolling across an empty crosswalk.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Which two mobility aids identify a pedestrian who is likely blind and needs extra driver caution?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Quiet hybrid or electric drivetrains give zero engine noise cues to someone navigating intersections by sound.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: How does Iowa traffic law frame right-of-way when road users meet without signs or signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Framing statutes around who must wait stops aggressive drivers from claiming legal permission to barrel forward.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What overriding duty applies even when the other driver or walker clearly should have yielded to you?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Being technically right on paper never repairs crumpled sheet metal or heals an injured pedestrian.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How do Iowa's statutory yield rules pair with every driver's duty to prevent a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Exam questions reject any answer choice where a driver insists on taking right-of-way into danger.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Why should you yield to a bicyclist even when traffic rules say the rider ought to wait for you?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: A sedan has crumple zones and airbags, whereas a cyclist absorbs every mistake directly on pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: What explains giving extra defensive leeway to cyclists who hold the exact same legal duties as cars?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Defensive drivers yield spare seconds whenever steel meets an unarmored bicycle frame at a corner.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Which single driving mistake causes more fatal traffic crashes in Iowa than any other?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Pulling across high-speed rural highways or oncoming left turns turns a split-second misjudgment fatal.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: What three conditions must all line up before you turn right at a steady red light?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Rolling a red right turn at five miles per hour skips the stop check that catches crosswalk joggers.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Who holds priority when you want to turn left across an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Cutting prematurely across fast straight-through headlights produces violent passenger-side broadside impacts inside open intersections.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How does what you wait for on a right-on-red turn compare with a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Right-on-red checks signs and cross gaps after halting, while unprotected lefts track oncoming closing speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: How do arrival order and tie-breakers work after stopping completely at an all-way stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Yielding to the driver on your right breaks deadlocks cleanly without hesitant bumper lurches.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What separates staggered arrivals from tied arrivals at an all-way stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Watching stop order as you roll up eliminates guesswork once four cars sit at the lines.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Who takes priority whenever your tires cross a sidewalk at an alley, lot, or driveway?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Hedges and garage walls hide dog walkers and kids on scooters until your bumper nears the walkway.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What is the legal difference between crossing a sidewalk and driving along one?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Concrete walkways are built solely for foot traffic apart from brief perpendicular driveway crossings.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Who gets priority when you pull onto a street from a shoulder, alley, or private driveway?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Through lanes move at full street pace and expect driveway mergers to wait for a safe gap.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Pulling out of a driveway across a sidewalk onto a street, which two yields happen back-to-back?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Treat leaving a parking lot as a two-stop sequence—before the concrete walkway, then again at the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Do pedestrian crosswalk rights depend on whether white lines are painted on the asphalt?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Every street corner forms a legal pedestrian corridor even where winter plows wore paint away.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How must you approach an intersection that has zero stop signs or traffic lights?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Tall summer cornfields along rural Iowa gravel roads turn unsigned crossroads lethal without early braking.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: What stays identical and what increases at an unsigned intersection compared with a signed one?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Without red octagons telling one road to halt, every approaching driver must verify cross traffic slows.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Which lights or sounds on police, fire, ambulance, or rescue vehicles trigger your duty to yield?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Spotting red or blue strobes in your mirror before hearing the siren gives extra seconds to clear lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: Where do you steer when an active emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Predictable rightward movement from every car opens a clean center lane for fast-moving responders.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: How do you handle an approaching emergency rig if you are mid-intersection or across a physical median?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Stopping inside a roundabout or crossroad corks turning room, while raised medians already separate opposing responders.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Why does pulling right immediately on an open street change to driving forward first inside an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Clearing the corner box ensures wide fire engines can swing onto any cross street unimpeded.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: What minimum distance must you keep behind an emergency vehicle running lights and siren?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Responders brake hard at unmarked scene addresses or hydrants without time for tailgaters to react.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Compare your duty across a median divider from an emergency rig against driving behind that same rig?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Physical medians shield opposite flow, whereas trailing in the same roadway demands a long safety buffer.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Following a school bus on a two- or three-lane road, what do flashing amber or red lamps forbid?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Trying to zip past an amber-flashing bus puts your car beside the door right as students step down.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: How far behind a stopped school bus with its arm extended must you halt, and when may you move?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Notice Iowa requires waiting until BOTH the stop arm folds in and the bus starts rolling again.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Meeting an oncoming school bus flashing amber lights on an undivided two- or three-lane road, what speed cap applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Iowa's specific twenty-mile-per-hour oncoming amber rule is a classic state-specific permit-test question.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: When that oncoming bus on a two- or three-lane road extends its stop arm, what must you do?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Children cross in front of the yellow hood across oncoming lanes, requiring a dead stop until the arm folds.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: How do amber school-bus lights restrict a trailing driver differently from an oncoming driver?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Behind the bus you cannot overtake at all, while approaching head-on caps your speed as you prepare to halt.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: How long can Iowa suspend your driver's license for illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Half a year without driving privileges underscores how fiercely Iowa protects students at bus stops.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: Pair the minimum stopping distance behind a school bus with the maximum license suspension for violating it?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Locking both numbers together nails two of Iowa's highest-yield school-bus exam questions.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: Does adding four or more lanes change your stopping duty when you are traveling behind a school bus?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Never use an open adjacent left lane to zip past a school bus going your direction.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: What is the single situation in Iowa where you may pass a stopped school bus with its arm out?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Students are never routed across four or more lanes of traffic, making oncoming four-lane flow Iowa's lone exception.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: Meeting an oncoming armed school bus, how does moving from three lanes to four lanes flip Iowa's rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Count total travel lanes carefully on test diagrams because four lanes is the exact cutoff for oncoming cars.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: On a four-lane road, why does one side stop for an armed school bus while the opposite side keeps rolling?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Students step directly onto the right-hand curb on the bus's side without ever crossing four lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: When does safe driving begin, and what guide sets your vehicle's maintenance schedule?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Catching worn parts in the driveway prevents sudden mechanical failures on seventy-mile-per-hour interstates.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How many independent brake systems must cars, trucks, and ATVs or UTVs have versus motorcycles and mopeds?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Separate foot and parking brakes ensure a ruptured hydraulic line still leaves mechanical cable stopping power.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Which four brake warning signs mean your vehicle needs a mechanic right away?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Squealing pads, burning smells, or spongy pedals warn that stopping power is failing fast.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Pair what guides routine vehicle maintenance with how brake-system requirements split by vehicle type?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Knowing both maintenance scheduling and equipment statutes covers common readiness test items.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: When brakes grind, smell odd, or sink underfoot, what is the single safe move?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Driving another week on failing hydraulics turns a simple pad-and-fluid service into a rear-end wreck.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: How do you confirm that headlights, taillights, brake lamps, and turn signals actually light up?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Dashboard indicators never reveal a burned-out brake bulb until you check outside or reflect off a wall.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What front, rear, and license-plate lights must every car, truck, and street-used ATV or UTV carry?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: A burned-out white tag bulb or dim red taillight invites both nighttime rear-enders and equipment stops.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What applies to any installed turn signals, and at what vehicle or trailer width are electric signals mandatory?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Wide trailers block hand gestures completely, making functioning electric blinkers required past forty inches.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: What two clues tell you a headlight is aimed crookedly, and who should fix it?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: If oncoming drivers flash high beams while yours are already on low, misaligned housings are blinding them.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: By how much can road grime cut your lamp brightness if you skip washing lenses?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Winter slush cakes clear plastic housings fast, cutting visibility in half until wiped clean.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Combine how you inspect exterior bulbs with the required lamp count on four-wheel vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: One quick walk around the bumpers checks both front beams, the rear red lamp, and the tag light.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Compare the rule for factory-installed blinkers against Iowa's width threshold requiring signals?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Even on a narrow rig where signals were optional, broken factory lamps still fail inspection.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Which headlight problem calls for a mechanic, and which one just needs soap and water?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Wiping winter salt off lenses takes thirty seconds at a gas pump before paying for alignment.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: How should you maintain windshields regarding cracks, glare film, and winter washer reservoirs?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Summer water freezes solid inside nozzles on January mornings right when salt spray blinds your glass.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: What winter clearing and wiper upkeep are required before pulling onto Iowa roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Peering through a postcard-sized hole scraped in frost hides cross traffic and pedestrians completely.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: How much light must pass through Iowa windshields and front side windows, and do medical waivers exist?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Iowa's strict rule banning even medical tint exemptions on front glass is a classic state-specific test trap.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What two interior and glass clutter habits must you avoid to keep a clear view?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Dangling tassels and windshield stickers swing across eye height right where distant cyclists appear.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How do you treat cracked auto glass differently from intact auto glass?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Pitted or spider-webbed safety glass scatters oncoming headlights into blinding halos and shatters easily.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Pair your winter window-clearing duties with Iowa's front-glass tint requirement?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Both rules serve one purpose so drivers and officers maintain clear two-way visibility year-round.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How do bald or unbalanced tires hurt safety and fuel economy, and what ride symptoms need a shop?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Smooth rubber surfs atop shallow rainwater while wheel shimmy or pulling warns of alignment or belt trouble.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: When should you gauge tire inflation, and where do you find the right pressure number?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Sidewall moldings list maximum tire ratings rather than your car's engineered pressure on the door jamb.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: How do you use a penny to tell whether tire tread is worn past safe limits?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Seeing the whole top of Abe's head means shallow grooves can no longer channel rain away from the road.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: Contrast how you check tire air pressure with how you check tire tread depth?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Five minutes once a month with a pocket gauge and a coin prevents blowouts and hydroplaning.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: Distinguish what bald tread causes on wet roads from what bouncing or side-pulling indicates?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Fresh rubber cures shallow grooves, whereas shakes and pulls demand balancing or suspension repair.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What should you do if your steering suddenly feels heavy, stiff, or slow to respond?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Worn tie rods or leaking power-steering racks can snap completely if ignored until a highway curve.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What worn components are likely to blame if your car keeps bouncing up and down after a bump or stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Tired dampers let tires hop off rough pavement, lengthening braking distances on washboard curves.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Match sluggish wheel response and non-stop bouncing after dips to their underlying systems?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Diagnostic test questions pair handling symptoms directly with steering linkage versus suspension shocks.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: What three jobs does the exhaust system perform, and why must you never idle inside a garage or sealed car?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Carbon monoxide has zero smell or color, putting occupants to sleep permanently inside closed spaces.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: Why is warming up an engine inside a garage forbidden?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Toxic fumes accumulate rapidly inside attached garages and seep into living spaces before engines even warm.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What road hazard and everyday costs come from an out-of-tune engine, and what guides its upkeep?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: A misfiring engine dying mid-left-turn across oncoming traffic turns neglected tune-ups into a crash hazard.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: For what sole purpose should you press your vehicle's horn?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Venting anger on the horn startles nearby pedestrians and drowns out genuine hazard alerts.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: Pair how you maintain a rough engine with the single legitimate reason to sound your horn?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Reliable power keeps you moving out of trouble while disciplined horn taps alert distracted neighbors.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: How far behind must your center mirror show, and when are outside mirrors mandatory?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Cargo boxes or packed vacation trunks block rear glass, shifting legal sight duties onto side mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: When must you adjust the driver's seat and mirrors to fit your frame?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Trying to slide a seat latch while rolling across a parking lot can jam your foot onto the gas.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: How far must your breastbone sit from the steering hub, and where should the wheel aim?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Airbags punch outward at explosive speed and need full inflation room before cushioning your torso.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: How high should the top of the wheel sit, how does your right foot pivot, and how do shorter drivers keep ten inches?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Planting your right heel lets your ankle pivot crisply from gas to brake without lifting your leg.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: How high should you set your seat's head restraint behind your skull?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: A headrest left down behind your neck acts like a fulcrum during a rear-end hit instead of catching your head.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: How should you posture and aim your inside rearview mirror?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Adjusting the mirror while slouched aims it at the ceiling once you sit upright on the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: How do you lean and aim the left side mirror to minimize blind spots?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Pushing side mirrors outward until painted doors disappear upright eliminates overlapping views and shrinks blind zones.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Where do you lean your head to set the passenger-side outside mirror?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Aiming from above the center console pushes the right glass wide enough to catch overtaking lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: Pair the required sight distance of an inside mirror with the special mirror rule for vans?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Panel vans carry wide rear pillars, making dual exterior mirrors mandatory regardless of rear glass.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: Combine your minimum chest-to-wheel clearance with Iowa's blind-zone mirror adjustment method?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Pairing safe airbag spacing with wide-angled side mirrors protects both crash survival and lane-change sight.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Why must you still know how to drive unassisted even with modern safety features?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Sensors fail in slush, need manual shutoff, or disappear completely when you borrow another car.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: How does Iowa's driving test separate safety helpers from convenience helpers?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Examiners welcome backup cameras yet ban adaptive cruise because you must prove your own skill.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which camera, detection, speed, and lane warning systems may stay active during your driving test?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Cameras, blind-spot monitors, lane-departure chimes, and cross-traffic alerts leave every steering input to you.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Which four acting assists are allowed on test day, and which two convenience systems are banned?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Emergency braking and lane keeping guard emergencies whereas auto-parking and adaptive cruise replace core skills.
sec09-card-sec09-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Four crash-assists in, two conveniences out

visual_sync.text_span: Four crash-assists in, two conveniences out

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Why does test day allow a backup camera while banning adaptive cruise control?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Safety helpers support hazard awareness whereas convenience features take over testable speed-spacing duties.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does the broad list of test-day warnings compare in count with approved acting assists?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Nearly every passive chime passes muster while only four emergency-acting assists stay legal.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Why does Iowa ban every convenience feature during the behind-the-wheel driving test?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Licensing examiners score your footwork and steering rather than your car's self-parking computer.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What two resources should you use to master every new assistance feature on your vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Dashboard icons and shutoff buttons vary wildly across brands until you read the manual.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: How do convenience-feature bans on test day pair with owner-manual study beforehand?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Knowing how to switch convenience tech off before the examiner boards saves awkward delays.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What do warning systems do when danger approaches, and who must execute the save?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Waiting for a dashboard beep to hit the brakes for you ends in impact.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: In the partnership between warning systems and the human driver, who plays which role?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Passive alerts buy split-second awareness, yet only your hands and feet steer clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Where do backup warnings scan, and which four checks must you still perform?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Ultrasonic bumper sensors can miss thin poles or darting kids outside their narrow cone.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: How do blind-spot monitors react when you signal toward a hidden car, and what checks remain?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Fast-closing motorcycles in adjacent lanes can outrun radar sensors without a shoulder glance.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How does the scanning zone of a backup warning differ from a blind-spot warning?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Reverse alerts guard backing paths whereas blind-spot icons guard sideways highway lane shifts.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Where do rear cameras display a wide view in reverse, and what do they never replace?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Staring exclusively at a dashboard screen misses cross-sidewalk bicycles approaching your rear fenders.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What triggers a sideview camera feed, when might it shut off, and what checks remain?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Because sideview feeds can sleep in reverse or at speed, mirror-and-shoulder habits stay mandatory.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Which four camera angles fuse into surround-view parking, and what checks still pair with it?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Overhead stitched views help tight curb alignment while mirrors and head turns spot moving traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How do rear cameras and sideview cameras differ in trigger and direction?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Shifting into reverse wakes the rear lens while flicking the turn stalk wakes sideview.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: How does a sideview camera stream compare with a surround-view camera display?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Sideview watches one adjacent lane whereas surround-view stitches four lenses for low-speed parking.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Near what speed do pedestrian, cyclist, and obstacle alerts work, and why scan downtown yourself?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Many sensors spot only straight-ahead same-direction targets and miss jaywalkers stepping from curbs.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: How do radar closing-gap chimes change rhythm as your bumper nears an obstacle?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Faster beeps turning into one continuous tone scream that collision is inches away.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: How do curve-speed warnings know an upcoming bend is too sharp for your pace?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Map data flags fast exit-ramp entries, yet wet leaves still demand slower driver judgment.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What basic upkeep keeps radar and camera sensors able to detect anything at all?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Road salt, mud, or winter slush smeared over bumper sensors blinds warnings completely.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: How do low-speed obstacle detection alerts differ from GPS curve-speed warnings?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Obstacle sensors watch city streets near twenty-five while GPS curve alerts watch fast ramps.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: What do faster radar beeps tell you, and what makes warning sensors go silent?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Silence never guarantees a clear bumper when winter road grime cakes your sensors.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What do forward crash-warning systems do and NOT do when traffic slows ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Forward crash warnings only sound the alarm, leaving braking or steering entirely to you.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: How fast and far does forward crash warning scan, and how many seconds ahead across three speed bands?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Scanning five hundred feet twenty times a second gives three, four, or five warning seconds.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What pedal action does forward crash warning skip despite sweeping five hundred feet twenty times per second?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Long five-hundred-foot radar reach buys reaction time only if your own foot hits brakes.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How should your foot respond when a GPS speeding alert chimes or flashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Slamming brakes for a minor speed chime shocks trailing traffic into rear-ending you.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What road markings power lane-departure warnings, and do those warnings steer your car?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Lane-departure alerts buzz when tires touch paint without moving the steering wheel one inch.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: What response fits a speeding alert, and what road cue powers a lane-departure warning?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Smooth throttle lifts fix excess pace while clear stripe paint feeds drift chimes.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What blind spots hamper parking sensors, and how do rear cross-traffic alerts help in lots?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Bumper sensors miss low curbs while cross-traffic radar spots aisle cars hidden behind SUVs.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: How do targets differ between bumper parking sensors and rear cross-traffic alerts?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Parking tones measure still posts behind you while cross-traffic watches moving cars sideways.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: How do assist systems step beyond passive warning systems, and why stay ready?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Assist tech shares physical braking or steering inputs yet still needs human backup.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: What single line separates passive warning systems from active assist systems?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Knowing whether your car merely beeps or applies brakes prevents fatal hesitation.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: When does automatic emergency braking step in, and what habits remain yours?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Relying on last-ditch auto-braking instead of safe following gaps risks high-speed impacts.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What two-stage sequence does automatic reverse braking run when an obstacle blocks your tail?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Even with auto-reverse braking aboard, checking mirrors and turning your head stay essential.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: How does lane-keeping assist work, and what three line conditions make it quit?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Faded paint, snow cover, or mud erases lane stripes and drops steering nudges cold.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: How does left-turn crash avoidance intervene if you start turning across oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: It blocks slow left-turn T-bones in tight gaps, yet turn judgment remains yours.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: How does automatic reverse braking's intervention differ from lane-keeping assist's intervention?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: One clamps brakes behind your bumper while the other guides steering between stripes.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: What road surface defeats lane-keeping assist, and what mistake triggers left-turn avoidance?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Worn winter stripes blind lane cameras whereas short oncoming gaps trigger left-turn braking.
sec09-card-sec09-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Faint stripes quit, short lefts freeze

visual_sync.text_span: Faint stripes quit, short lefts freeze

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: What does adaptive cruise control manage in traffic, and when should you rest it?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Rain, snow, or ice fools radar pacing and can spin tires under automated throttle.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: How do car and driver split duties during automatic parallel parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Even while steering spins hands-free into the curb, braking and scanning stay yours.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: How do adaptive cruise control and automatic parallel parking split work with the driver?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Both convenience helpers demand alert supervision and stay completely off during driving tests.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: How strictly does Iowa enforce and punish alcohol- or drug-impaired driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Troopers prioritize impaired-driving stops above routine violations to prevent fatal highway collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: What blood-alcohol level or drug presence defines Operating While Intoxicated, and which three samples prove it?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Even trace amounts of a controlled substance trigger OWI without a single drop of alcohol.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How does Iowa's enforcement priority pair with the two-part legal trigger for OWI?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Heavy roadside patrols enforce both the point-zero-eight alcohol ceiling and zero-tolerance drug rules.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: How many days of driving privileges can you still lose despite a criminal-court acquittal?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Administrative license revocation runs separately from criminal verdicts and stretches longer on repeat arrests.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Why does winning in criminal court fail to save privileges, and what do repeat OWI arrests do?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Iowa's licensing agency revokes privileges for six months minimum regardless of courtroom outcomes.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: What sobriety-check agreement comes built into holding an Iowa license or driving through as a visitor?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Driving on Iowa roads automatically binds both residents and out-of-state visitors to officer checks.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Does refusing a breathalyzer save you, and what revocation and minimum fine hit automatically?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Refusing chemical sampling carries harsher automatic license loss than failing the breathalyzer outright.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Which two extra requirements can follow a breathalyzer-refusal conviction in Iowa?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Offenders pay out of pocket for substance-use evaluations and ignition-interlock hardware before driving.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: Who falls under Iowa implied consent, and how does refusing compare with failing?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Both locals and visitors consent by driving, and refusal triggers a year off plus twelve-fifty.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: At what blood-alcohol level do underage drivers hit OWI, and how long are the two revocation tiers?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Barely measurable alcohol costs sixty days underage while hitting point-zero-eight triples revocation length.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: Can an offender under age eighteen obtain a temporary restricted license during an OWI revocation?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Adults sometimes qualify for work permits whereas minors sit out every single revoked day.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: How does an underage driver's revocation jump between point-zero-two and point-zero-eight BAC?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Crossing from underage trace alcohol into adult intoxication triples minimum revocation days.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Where may an open alcohol container legally ride, and what fine hits cabin violations?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Even sober drivers get cited up to two hundred dollars when passengers hold open cans.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How does Iowa treat open alcohol inside the passenger cabin compared with the trunk?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Stowing resealed bottles inside the trunk spares both driver and passengers misdemeanor fines.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: In what four dangerous ways does drowsy driving mirror drunk driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Sleep-deprived brains lag on pedals and drift across shoulders just like intoxicated ones.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Which five mental or physical warning signs show drowsiness creeping in?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Realizing you cannot recall the last few highway miles means microsleeps already started.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Which five driving behaviors signal road drowsiness, and what three fixes answer them?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Hitting shoulder rumble strips or tailgating unconsciously demands an immediate safe pullover.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What blood-alcohol level matches the impairment of staying awake eighteen straight hours?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Pulling an eighteen-hour day before driving home impairs you like legal intoxication.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How deadly is drowsy driving, and which early mental clues warn you first?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Catching daydreams, yawns, and forgotten miles early lets you stop before drifting off-road.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How do lane-drift and rumble-strip warnings pair with Iowa's eighteen-waking-hour benchmark?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Once awake eighteen hours, your crash odds rival a driver blowing point zero eight.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Which three road-blocking surprises should you plan around before every short or long trip?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Even familiar daily commutes turn hazardous when blizzards, orange barrels, or pileups hit.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Which state website and mobile app report live Iowa highway and interstate conditions?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Checking Iowa five-one-one before winter trips spots closed interstates while still parked home.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: How do weather, construction, and crash checks pair with Iowa's five-one-one tools?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Two minutes on the free five-one-one app routes you cleanly around storms and closures.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: How do core driving fundamentals apply once you move from basic streets to complex roads, weather, and emergencies?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Scanning, speed control, and yielding stay identical even when interchange layouts or rural surfaces look unfamiliar.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: Which everyday driveways, lots, and road junctions all count as intersections?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Treating parking-lot exits, alleys, and private driveways with full intersection alertness catches pull-out cars early.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: Walk through the three ordered looks for approaching and entering an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Looking left first and left again last checks the closest cross-traffic lane right before your nose enters.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Why must you wait until an approaching vehicle actually begins turning instead of trusting its turn signal?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Drivers signal for driveways beyond you or forget stuck blinkers, especially motorcycles whose signals often lack auto-cancel.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: Combine what counts as an intersection with the three-step visual scan used at each one?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Running controls, path, and left-right-left at driveways as well as cross streets eliminates surprise T-bones.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: How do assuming zero courtesy and distrusting lit turn signals protect you at corners?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Pulling out on faith because a blinker flashed puts fault and side-impact steel squarely on your door.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: How do you cross a four-lane divided rural highway in two stages using the median?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Judging one fast direction at a time beats trying to thread four highway lanes in one risky dash.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: What two hazards arise from high rural speeds and narrow highway medians when long vehicles cross?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: A pickup towing a boat or trailer can stick out into live sixty-five-mile-per-hour lanes if the median is narrow.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: How does two-gap median crossing pair with watching median width for long rigs?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Passenger cars pause safely inside wide medians, while long combinations must wait until both directions clear if narrow.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: How do the entrance, acceleration, and merge zones of a highway on-ramp work, and what do through drivers do?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Matching highway speed on the acceleration lane lets you blend smoothly while mainline cars shift left when clear.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: How do entering ramp drivers and current highway drivers share a smooth merge?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Stopping needlessly on an on-ramp wrecks merge momentum and surprises drivers accelerating behind you.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: How does a reduced-conflict intersection replace a direct side-road left turn across four lanes?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Handling one direction of fast traffic at a time eliminates deadly right-angle broadside crashes on rural expressways.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: What dangerous two-way wait disappears at a reduced-conflict J-turn intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Instead of judging simultaneous left and right highway gaps from a dead stop, you blend right and U-turn cleanly.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: What unusual lane shift happens inside a diverging diamond interchange, and what traffic benefit does it create?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Shifting traffic temporarily to the left side lets freeway ramps turn left without crossing oncoming lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: Why does a diverging diamond route traffic briefly to the opposite side of the overpass?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Signs, signals, and high-curb islands guide you cleanly onto the left and right back again without conflict.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: Which direction does traffic circle inside a roundabout, and what controls entry instead of stoplights?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Slow curved entries and counterclockwise flow around a central island eliminate high-speed head-on and T-bone angles.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What two yields happen in sequence as you enter a single-lane roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Stopping across the crosswalk while peeking left into the circle blocks pedestrians and cyclists crossing the leg.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: How do you drive inside a single-lane roundabout and exit cleanly?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Signaling right tells waiting drivers you are peeling off so traffic flows smoothly while you watch the exit crosswalk.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: How do pedestrians cross a roundabout leg safely using the raised splitter island?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Splitter islands divide crossing into two short one-direction checks away from the circulating ring.
sec15-card-sec15-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Look left, pause island, look right

visual_sync.text_span: Look left, pause island, look right

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: What two options do cyclists have for navigating a roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Experienced riders who stay on the road claim the middle of the lane rather than hugging the curb where cars peel off.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: Why do roundabouts keep moving without stop signs, and who holds priority over entering cars?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Both crosswalk users and vehicles already circling inside outrank drivers waiting behind the shark-tooth yield line.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: Summarize how cars exit, pedestrians cross, and cyclists ride or walk at single-lane roundabouts?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Every user gets dedicated space when drivers signal exits, walkers use splitter islands, and riding cyclists take full lanes.
sec15-card-sec15-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Blink right, use islands, claim center

visual_sync.text_span: Blink right, use islands, claim center

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: What four habits are essential when approaching and exiting a multi-lane roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Yielding to both circulating lanes and signaling right just past the exit before yours avoids cross-lane cutoffs.
sec15-card-sec15-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Pick lane early, yield both, blink

visual_sync.text_span: Pick lane early, yield both, blink

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What three mistakes are forbidden once you are inside a multi-lane roundabout?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Changing lanes mid-circle, riding beside wide-tracking semi-trailers, or turning left from an exit-only outer lane causes sideswipes.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: Where must pedestrians never walk at a roundabout, and why do raised truck aprons ring the center island?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Pedestrians cross only at perimeter splitter islands, while mountable concrete aprons let long trailer rear wheels track around.
sec15-card-sec15-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Skip center island, aprons serve trailers

visual_sync.text_span: Skip center island, aprons serve trailers

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: Combine what you must do before entering a multi-lane roundabout with what you must never do inside?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Pre-selecting the signed lane before entry removes any urge to weave or crowd semi-trucks inside the circle.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: How does loose gravel change tire grip, and what four adjustments keep control?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Marbles of loose stone roll under tires, so slower speed, gentle steering, soft braking, and wider gaps prevent ditch spins.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: Which five rural obstacles block intersection and driveway sightlines in farm country?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Tall summer cornfields, windbreaks, barns, hills, and gravel dust can hide a crossroad pickup completely until the corner.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: How do you approach an unsigned rural gravel intersection, and which vehicle yields?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Never trust absence of dust to mean clear roads, and remember the driver on the left yields to the right.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: What happens if tires drop onto a soft rural shoulder, and how should you pass oncoming vehicles there?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Loose turf or mud grabs right-side tires hard, so slow well down before edging right past wide oncoming rigs.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: Which headlight setting helps other drivers see you through thick gravel dust?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Low beams pierce airborne dust without glaring back in your face while lighting your taillights for followers.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: Why are rural gravel roads a double hazard of traction and sightlines?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Needing longer distance to stop on gravel right where tall crops hide cross traffic demands early slowdowns.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: Tie together Iowa's unsigned-gravel yield rule, soft-shoulder hazard, and dust headlight rule?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Those three habits cover the biggest causes of rural Iowa rollovers and crossroad T-bone crashes.
sec15-card-sec15-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Yield right, respect shoulders, low beams

visual_sync.text_span: Yield right, respect shoulders, low beams

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What five kinds of roadway info do traffic signs share, and how do shape and color help you?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Even through snow, glare, or distance, a road sign's silhouette and background color reveal its category before words appear.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: What three types of driver action does the color red command on a roadway sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Red always signals an urgent restriction or halt, never a casual suggestion you can roll past.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: What navigation details does a green background provide on highway signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Scanning green panels early lets you line up lane changes smoothly before reaching your exit or city turnoff.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Which roadside traveler needs and destinations are marked by blue traffic signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Spotting blue panels helps tired or low-fuel motorists exit safely for gas, food, lodging, rest areas, or hospitals.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: What kind of destinations do brown roadway signs guide drivers toward?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Test questions mix up blue services with brown panels, which strictly mark recreational parks and cultural or historic sites.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: What message category does a standard yellow background communicate on a road sign?
