visual_sync.text_span: Broken white or dashed yellow side

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: What does a double solid yellow center line forbid, and how do yellow and white lines split traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Yellow always warns that the adjacent lane travels toward you, whereas white divides lanes moving together.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: Compare passing rules across broken white, mixed solid-broken yellow, and double solid yellow lines?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Reading both color and dash pattern tells you instantly whether overtaking is open, one-sided, or closed.
sec13-card-sec13-R13.must_match_memory_hook: White passes, dashed passes, double blocks

visual_sync.text_span: White passes, dashed passes, double blocks

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: What two terrain features forbid passing because they hide oncoming traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Crests and blind bends conceal oncoming vehicles closing at over a hundred combined miles per hour.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: Within one hundred feet of which five roadway structures or crossings is passing illegal in Iowa?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Narrow bridges, viaducts, tunnels, rail tracks, and intersections pinch lanes or add cross traffic with zero escape shoulder.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What side is off-limits for passing, and how should you treat questionable oncoming gaps?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Dropping onto shoulders to pass right or gambling on tight oncoming space turns impatience into head-on wrecks.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: Group Iowa's terrain bans, hundred-foot structure bans, and side-or-gap passing bans together?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: Locking in one hundred feet alongside hills, curves, and no-right-passing covers every passing-ban exam question.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: What percentage of serious crashes stem from human choices or mistakes, making defensive driving essential?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Because driver error drives nearly nineteen out of twenty serious wrecks, staying alert and proactive prevents almost all of them.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: What actions define the first defensive driving habit of thinking safety first?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Dropping aggressive or distracted impulses while keeping front space and seat belts buckled builds your baseline crash shield.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: How far ahead in seconds should you read traffic, and how should your eyes work to stay aware?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Checking mirrors frequently while sweeping twenty to thirty seconds ahead spots slowdowns blocks before you reach them.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: How should you respond to an aggressive driver, and which vulnerable users must stay on your radar?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Letting an aggressive driver pass by slowing, pulling over, or exiting ends conflict while keeping focus on walkers, bikes, and wildlife.
sec14-card-sec14-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Give space, pull off, watch walkers

visual_sync.text_span: Give space, pull off, watch walkers

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: What does the third defensive habit say about trusting other drivers at red lights and stop signs?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Planning for a cross-street car to blow its red light or stop sign saves you from broadside intersection hits.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: How many seconds of following distance does Iowa's fourth defensive habit recommend?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Three to four seconds gives your eyes and brakes real time to absorb sudden stops without chain-reaction hits.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: Why must you cut speed below posted limits when road or weather conditions deteriorate?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Posted signs reflect dry ideal pavement, and extra speed strips away steering and braking control when hazards appear.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: What does banking an escape route mean for positioning your vehicle in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Positioning where drivers see you and keeping an open side lane or shoulder gives you somewhere to steer if lanes jam.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: What does the seventh defensive driving habit require regarding distractions?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Split-second phone, food, or screen glances erase every space and scanning advantage you built.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: How does the ninety-four-percent human-error crash statistic connect to safety-first habits?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Since mechanical failures rarely cause serious wrecks, buckling up and banking space directly counters human mistakes.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: How do twenty-to-thirty-second visual scans pair with stepping aside from aggressive drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Seeing erratic weavers early in your mirrors or ahead gives you plenty of room to ease away calmly.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How do expecting stop-sign runners and holding a three-to-four-second gap reinforce each other?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Healthy skepticism spots cross-traffic errors while your following gap keeps trailing space open when you brake.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: Which three habits finish the defensive list, and why is obeying speed signs alone not enough?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Driving the posted limit blindly while boxed in or distracted still leaves you trapped when conditions turn slick.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Why is driving at a uniform lawful pace with surrounding traffic safer than going much faster or slower?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Big speed gaps trigger constant lane swaps, close tailgating, and risky passes that multiply collision points.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: How should you adjust when you spot slower traffic ahead instead of waiting until the last moment?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Changing lanes early or easing speed gradually keeps trailing cars from piling into your rear bumper.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Which five types of slow-moving vehicles appear on Iowa roads, and what warning emblems or lights mark them?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Tractors, buggies, ATVs, UTVs, and maintenance rigs often crawl under twenty-five, closing highway gaps shockingly fast.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: Why is tailgating dangerous, and how should your following count change as speeds climb?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Riding bumpers erases stopping margin, so start at three to four seconds and add extra seconds on fast highways.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: What four calm steps help shake a tailgater riding closely behind you?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Easing right lets the follower see past your car, and signaling early or slowing gently invites a clean pass.
sec14-card-sec14-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Edge right, signal early, let pass

visual_sync.text_span: Edge right, signal early, let pass

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: What happens to crash risk when everyone holds a uniform lawful speed versus driving as an outlier?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Smooth uniform flow keeps spacing predictable instead of forcing constant overtaking maneuvers.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: Why must you spot orange slow-moving triangles or rear flashers from far back on rural highways?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Closing at fifty-five on a fifteen-mile-per-hour tractor feels almost like approaching a parked vehicle.
sec14-card-sec14-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Spot triangles early, avoid hard stops

visual_sync.text_span: Spot triangles early, avoid hard stops

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: How do you prevent tailgating ahead while managing someone tailgating behind?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Keeping generous front space guarantees you never have to slam brakes with a close follower glued to your trunk.
sec14-card-sec14-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Hold four ahead, invite pass behind

visual_sync.text_span: Hold four ahead, invite pass behind

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: What two things must every driver communicate to surrounding traffic, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Crashes happen when another road user either never saw you there or never expected your sudden turn or stop.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Why must you turn headlights on manually during daytime fog, rain, or bright snow glare?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Bright daytime fog or snow tricks automatic light sensors into leaving your taillights and low beams dark.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: At what times, visibility footage, and wiper use does Iowa law require both headlights on?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Memorize five hundred feet alongside sunset-to-sunrise and wipers-on as Iowa's three mandatory headlight triggers.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Which four situations involving drifting walkers, passers, distracted drivers, or blind alleys call for your horn?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: A timely horn tap alerts someone stepping off a curb, drifting into your lane, or hidden past an alley wall.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: What three additional danger situations, including losing control of your own car, call for sounding the horn?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Blasting the horn if your car slides out of control gives pedestrians or cyclists precious seconds to jump clear.
sec14-card-sec14-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Sound horn for threats or skids

visual_sync.text_span: Sound horn for threats or skids

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: If your vehicle breaks down, how do you position and light it, and which terrain spots must you avoid?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Parking just beyond a hilltop or bend hides your four-way flashers until oncoming traffic cannot stop in time.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: If your vehicle stalls dead inside a moving travel lane and cannot roll off, what must everyone do?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: A dead car sitting in a live lane is a high-speed impact magnet, so get occupants well clear of the road and shoulder.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: How does broadcasting presence and plans tie directly to daytime weather headlight use?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: White cars in snow or gray cars in rain vanish without manual headlights and taillights lit.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: Combine Iowa's mandatory headlight triggers with the purpose of its seven horn-warning scenarios?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Lights handle continuous visibility under five hundred feet while the horn handles sudden human blind spots.
sec14-card-sec14-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred sight, horn prevents strikes

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred sight, horn prevents strikes

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: How does handling a breakdown that reaches the roadside differ from a car stuck inside a travel lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Getting clear of lanes buys breathing room with hazards on, whereas a blocked live lane demands immediate evacuation far off-road.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: How should you pass oncoming vehicles on a narrow unmarked rural gravel road?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Center ruts lure both cars toward the middle on unpainted gravel, so easing right early prevents mirror strikes in dust.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: Why must you approach rural bridges ready to stop before crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Many older country bridges pinch narrower than the gravel road itself and fit only one vehicle across at once.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: Compare meeting oncoming traffic on open narrow gravel against meeting traffic at a narrow rural bridge?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Open gravel lets two slowed cars pass carefully, whereas a one-vehicle bridge requires yielding before the deck.
sec16-card-sec16-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Gravel hugs right, narrow bridge waits

visual_sync.text_span: Gravel hugs right, narrow bridge waits

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: How do off-highway rural hills and curves differ from main highways, and what should you do beforehand?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Secondary rural crests and bends are built steeper and tighter, hiding oncoming pickups drifting across unpainted centers.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: Why must you slow, look both ways, and be ready to stop at rural railroad crossings?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Most country rail crossings lack active flashing lights, bells, gates, or pavement paint to announce approaching trains.
sec16-card-sec16-F04.must_match_memory_hook: No gates or bells, look twice

visual_sync.text_span: No gates or bells, look twice

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: Pair your approach to steep rural crests and curves with your approach to bare country railroad crossings?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Both rural spots lack modern highway buffers, putting all safety weight on early speed drops and active looking.
sec16-card-sec16-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Slow right at crests, scan tracks

visual_sync.text_span: Slow right at crests, scan tracks

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: Why does overtaking wide farm machinery require extreme caution even on an open rural stretch?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Combines and tractors span beyond lane width, hide small blinkers under dust, and often swing wide before field left turns.
sec16-card-sec16-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Watch wide implements and left turns

visual_sync.text_span: Watch wide implements and left turns

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: What speed, gap, mirror, headlight, and eye habits keep driving safe after dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Flipping your rearview mirror to night mode and looking toward the right edge line defeats blinding headlight glare.
sec16-card-sec16-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Slow, widen gaps, track right stripe

visual_sync.text_span: Slow, widen gaps, track right stripe

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: Contrast what protects you around slow rural machinery with what protects you against night glare?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Daytime rural hazards demand watching wide implements, while nighttime hazards demand low-beam etiquette and edge-line tracking.
sec16-card-sec16-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Spot tractors early, track edge stripe

visual_sync.text_span: Spot tractors early, track edge stripe

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: When are animals most active, and why should you hold your lane instead of swerving if you cannot stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Violent swerves for deer launch cars into oncoming traffic, trees, or ditch rollovers far deadlier than a straight strike.
sec16-card-sec16-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Dawn-dusk peak, brake straight, never swerve

visual_sync.text_span: Dawn-dusk peak, brake straight, never swerve

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: Which animal leads Iowa wildlife crashes, which three months peak, and why keep scanning after seeing one?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Fall rut and spring movement spike deer crossings, and deer travel in groups so a second or third often trails.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: Connect Iowa's peak deer months and dawn-dusk hours with the no-swerve survival rule?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Extra scanning in October, November, and May buys braking time, while holding straight prevents rollover swerves.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: Who suffers seventy-eight percent of deaths in large-truck crashes, and how do you check semi blind spots?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Passenger-car occupants absorb nearly four in five truck-crash fatalities, and front, rear, and side no-zones hide whole cars.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: Why do big trucks need far longer braking room, and when may you merge back in front of one?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Cutting tightly across a semi's front bumper steals the long stopping cushion eighty-thousand-pound rigs require.
sec16-card-sec16-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Wait for full cab in mirror

visual_sync.text_span: Wait for full cab in mirror

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: Why do right-turning semi-trucks swing left first, and what gap must you never squeeze into?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Long trailers track sharply inward across the right lane and curb, crushing any car that sneaks beside them.
sec16-card-sec16-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Never squeeze between truck and curb

visual_sync.text_span: Never squeeze between truck and curb

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: How does the seventy-eight-percent fatality stat explain staying clear of front, rear, and side no-zones?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: If you cannot see the trucker's side mirrors, the trucker cannot see your car beside or behind the trailer.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: Pair the rule for returning in front of a passed truck with the rule for right-turning trucks?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Both rules guard the two deadliest pinch zones around tractor-trailers on highways and city corners.
sec16-card-sec16-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Full nose mirror, clear right curb

visual_sync.text_span: Full nose mirror, clear right curb

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: Why are intersections high-risk for motorcycles, and why must you distrust a motorcycle's turn signal?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: A slim single headlight looks farther and slower than it really is, and many bike blinkers stay lit manually.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: What following gap does a motorcycle need, why add more in rain, and how much lane width does passing take?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Wet steel grates, gravel, or grooves can wobble two wheels unexpectedly, and lane-splitting beside a rider steals maneuvering room.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: Summarize intersection caution, following gap, and lane width when sharing roads with motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Giving riders full-car lane width and generous stopping seconds compensates for their quick braking and light profile.
sec16-card-sec16-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Verify turns, four seconds, full lane

visual_sync.text_span: Verify turns, four seconds, full lane

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: Which foot and wheeled users must you scan for and yield to at intersections and driveways?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Skaters, scooters, wheelchairs, and pedestrians enter crosswalks and sidewalk aprons at varying heights and speeds.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: Why must you never pass a vehicle stopped or slowing near a crosswalk?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Overtaking a stopped vehicle in the adjacent lane blindsides the pedestrian stepping past its front fender.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: Combine active driveway-and-corner scanning with the ban on passing stopped crosswalk vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Even when you cannot yet see why the next lane slowed at an intersection, assume a person is crossing.
sec16-card-sec16-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Scan every crossing, never pass stops

visual_sync.text_span: Scan every crossing, never pass stops

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: Why are bicycles riding in street lanes, and how must you pass and return around one?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Many cities ban sidewalk cycling, so treat cyclists as legitimate traffic and move completely into the next lane.
sec16-card-sec16-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Change lanes fully, mirror before return

visual_sync.text_span: Change lanes fully, mirror before return

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: When are bicyclists hardest to spot, and what maneuver demands an extra right-side blind-spot check?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Turning right across a straight-riding cyclist in your right blind spot causes classic right-hook intersection crashes.
sec16-card-sec16-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Watch night reflectors, check right turns

visual_sync.text_span: Watch night reflectors, check right turns

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: Tie together how you overtake a cyclist ahead and how you protect one before turning right?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Wide passing clearance and over-the-right-shoulder checks before turns prevent the two most common bike-car collisions.
sec16-card-sec16-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Full lane pass, check right blind

visual_sync.text_span: Full lane pass, check right blind

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: How hot can an enclosed cabin get within ten minutes or on a seventy-eight-degree day, and what rescue does Iowa allow?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Parked cars trap greenhouse heat fatally fast, so Iowa law permits breaking a window to save a person or pet.
sec16-card-sec16-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Over one-sixty fast, rescue glass legal

visual_sync.text_span: Over one-sixty fast, rescue glass legal

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: Who must never be left alone in an enclosed vehicle, and what two actions save someone trapped?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: Children, older adults, dependent persons, and pets suffer rapid heatstroke, so dial nine-one-one and provide medical rescue.
sec16-card-sec16-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Never leave anyone, call, break glass

visual_sync.text_span: Never leave anyone, call, break glass

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: How can you check real-time road and plow conditions across Iowa before starting a bad-weather trip?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Twenty-four-hour online and mobile plow-camera feeds reveal whiteouts or closures before you leave home.
sec16-card-sec16-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Check Iowa traveler app and cameras

visual_sync.text_span: Check Iowa traveler app and cameras

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: If you cannot postpone a storm drive, what five precautions protect you?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: Cruise control can spin tires wildly on slick patches, while a maintained car and winter kit cover strandings.
sec16-card-sec16-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Slow, widen gap, disable cruise, kit

visual_sync.text_span: Slow, widen gap, disable cruise, kit

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: Pair pre-trip weather scouting with your behind-the-wheel storm adjustments?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Checking cameras cancels unnecessary blizzard trips, and slow cruise-free driving protects unavoidable ones.
sec16-card-sec16-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Scout cameras first, kill cruise driving

visual_sync.text_span: Scout cameras first, kill cruise driving

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: What following gap, beam, cruise, defroster, and glance habits apply on wet pavement?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Rain stretches stopping distance so five-to-six-second gaps, clear defrosted glass, and zero cruise control keep tires planted.
sec16-card-sec16-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Five-to-six seconds, low beams, no cruise

visual_sync.text_span: Five-to-six seconds, low beams, no cruise

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: What causes tires to hydroplane, and what three visual road clues warn you to slow down?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Standing puddles, mirror-shiny asphalt, or disappearing tire tracks behind the car ahead mean water is wedging under rubber.
sec16-card-sec16-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Water deeper than tread lifts tires

visual_sync.text_span: Water deeper than tread lifts tires

sec16-card-sec16-R12.question_text: Connect Iowa's five-to-six-second wet following gap with what happens when water exceeds tread depth?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.teaching_text: Extra seconds keep you clear of panic braking right where standing water could plane your tires into a skid.
sec16-card-sec16-R12.must_match_memory_hook: Six-second rain gap, watch vanishing tracks

visual_sync.text_span: Six-second rain gap, watch vanishing tracks

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: How little moving water can sweep away even an SUV or pickup, and what if your car stalls in floodwater?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: Nearly half of flash-flood deaths happen in vehicles, so never cross flooded roads and abandon stalled cars for high ground.
sec16-card-sec16-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Six inches sweeps trucks, climb high

visual_sync.text_span: Six inches sweeps trucks, climb high

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: If floodwater sweeps your vehicle under water, what steps let you open the door and escape?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Outside water pressure pins doors shut until the interior floods enough to equalize pressure so you can push out and swim.
sec16-card-sec16-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Stay calm, equalize cabin, push out

visual_sync.text_span: Stay calm, equalize cabin, push out

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: Which lights work in fog, which lights must stay off, and when should you leave the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight off suspended fog droplets into a blinding white wall, and zero sight means parking off-road.
sec16-card-sec16-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Low or fog beams, never highs

visual_sync.text_span: Low or fog beams, never highs

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: How does a tornado watch differ from a tornado warning, and what is a driver's best shelter?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: Vehicles toss easily in twister winds, so head straight inside a sturdy building whenever sirens or warnings sound.
sec16-card-sec16-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Watch means possible, warning means imminent

visual_sync.text_span: Watch means possible, warning means imminent

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: If a tornado strikes on the open road with no building nearby, what are your two options and what structure is banned?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Highway overpasses funnel wind into deadly debris tunnels, whereas buckling below window height or lying in a low ditch shields you.
sec16-card-sec16-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Duck low or ditch, skip overpasses

visual_sync.text_span: Duck low or ditch, skip overpasses

sec16-card-sec16-R13.question_text: Review the key trap in flash floods, dense fog, and tornado alerts?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.teaching_text: Those three weather traps flip common instincts that overestimate heavy trucks, bright beams, and concrete bridges.
sec16-card-sec16-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Six-inch floods, low beams, skip overpasses

visual_sync.text_span: Six-inch floods, low beams, skip overpasses

sec16-card-sec16-F28.question_text: What must you clear off your vehicle before driving in winter, and why do bridges freeze before roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.teaching_text: Cold air chills bridge decks from both top and bottom, forming invisible black ice while ground-warmed asphalt stays wet.
sec16-card-sec16-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Clear all snow, bridges freeze first

visual_sync.text_span: Clear all snow, bridges freeze first

sec16-card-sec16-F29.question_text: How do you start moving and brake on snow or ice, and how much can icy stopping distance multiply?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.teaching_text: Stopping on ice can take ten times dry distance, so straighten wheels before gentle launching or early braking without cruise.
sec16-card-sec16-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Straight gentle inputs, up to tenfold

visual_sync.text_span: Straight gentle inputs, up to tenfold

sec16-card-sec16-R14.question_text: Combine full snow clearing, bridge black ice, and straight-wheel ice inputs?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.teaching_text: Seeing clearly and keeping tires pointed straight while accelerating or braking prevents sudden winter spinouts.
sec16-card-sec16-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Clean windows, watch bridges, steer straight

visual_sync.text_span: Clean windows, watch bridges, steer straight

sec16-card-sec16-F30.question_text: How fast do snowplows typically work, why never pass on the shoulder side, and what sticks out?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.teaching_text: Plows throw blinding snow clouds to the right with wide wing blades extending into shoulders and huge blind spots.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.question_text: If snow strands your car on the highway, where should you wait and what location clues help dispatchers?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.teaching_text: Walking into blowing snow quickly disorients and freezes people, whereas a belted cabin gives rescuers a visible target.
sec16-card-sec16-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Stay belted inside, call with mileposts

visual_sync.text_span: Stay belted inside, call with mileposts

sec16-card-sec16-R15.question_text: Pair safe spacing around slow snowplows with survival rules if a blizzard strands your car?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.teaching_text: Respecting thirty-mile-per-hour plow wings avoids collisions, and staying buckled inside keeps you safe if visibility hits zero.
sec16-card-sec16-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Give plows room, stay belted inside

visual_sync.text_span: Give plows room, stay belted inside

sec17-card-sec17-F01.question_text: Why must even careful defensive drivers know emergency maneuvers before trouble strikes?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.teaching_text: Blowouts, deer, or mechanical faults give seconds rather than minutes, so rehearsed instincts beat panic.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.question_text: What steering, throttle, and brake inputs bring a vehicle safely off the road after a blowout?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.teaching_text: Slamming brakes on a blown tire shifts weight forward and spins the rim into pavement.
sec17-card-sec17-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Grip straight, ease gas, feather brake

visual_sync.text_span: Grip straight, ease gas, feather brake

sec17-card-sec17-F03.question_text: Which way does a front-tire blowout pull your car, and what steering mistake must you resist?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel violently opposite the pull can snap the vehicle sideways across live lanes.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.question_text: Combine general blowout pedal control with the steering rule for a blown front tire?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.teaching_text: Smooth steering correction paired with gentle coasting gets even a shredded front tire onto the right shoulder.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.question_text: What switches and backup lamps should you try while pulling off if your headlights fail?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.teaching_text: Sometimes the high-beam circuit or fog lights still work on a separate fuse long enough to guide you off-road.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.question_text: Do steering and brakes stop working completely if your engine stalls in motion?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.teaching_text: Power assist drops out when the engine quits, so firm two-handed steering and hard foot pressure still stop you.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.question_text: Contrast your immediate actions when headlights go dark versus when the engine stalls?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.teaching_text: Both emergencies end on the shoulder, one using backup lighting circuits and the other using extra muscle.
